properties.comments: Path probably not continuous.

The tornado formed near the Kings Grant subdivision in Wilmington near Jamey Ct, then moved toward the northwest near West Gate Rd. There was some minor shingle damage to homes, but mostly large limbs were down along with a couple snapped/uprooted trees. The tornado crossed North Kerr Rd near a truck rental business, then moved across northeast portions of the Wilmington International Airport before causing additional tree damage along Cornelius Moor Ave and Acorn Branch Rd. The tornado lifted in the woods north of Acorn Branch Rd.

A tornado tracked SE with EF1 damage to a farmstead east of Reynolds and reports of a persistent funnel that may have caused minor damage before and after the listed track but no damage has been found or reported relating these funnels.
Nielsville FD reported multiple brief touchdowns near the pilling station lasting no more than 30 seconds and doing no reported damage other that stripping some leaves off crops

A tornado tracked NW to SE with a final S push as it occluded as it tracked for about 5.3 miles. This tornado mainly scoured a soybean/corn field before doing damage to some farm outbuildings. This track may be adjusted pending high resolution satellite imagery. UPDATE 7/22: Track adjusted based on Sentinel-2 imagery.

A large dusty tornado was reported near Calio ND with no damage conveyed from any sources who witnessed it. It is suspected that this was spawned out of landspout processes which likely contributed to its dusty tubelike appearance as seen on social media. UPDATE 7/22/25: Adjusted track based on Sentinel-2 satellite imagery.
Law enforcement reported a tornadic circulation in this location around 4:27pm with no damage reported.
Spotter reported a brief tornado 5mi NE of Lawton, ND with no damage reported
Spotter reported a weak ground circulation lasting for 1-2 minutes with no damage reported.

A weak, short-lived tornado briefly touched down in the Savannah National Wildlife Refuge, in southern Jasper County, SC. The tornado initiated just east of Plantation Island Trail, where it snapped some small tree limbs and tops of some trees. It moved toward the north-northwest, snapping more small tree limbs, before crossing Laurel Hill Wildlife Drive, ending just south of South Carolina State Road 170.

This short-lived tornado peeled a ~45 x 40 sheet metal section of an outbuilding roof and threw it over 100 yards into a corn field. There were also crop and minor tree damage, and a nearby billboard with some damage.

This tornado tracked through some rural residences and wooded areas near the Cedar River in far eastern Benton and far western Linn Counties. Damage was mainly to trees, including numerous uprooted or snapped, though a few homes and garages had roof damage. The tornado ended on the south end of Center Point. Within the town of Center Point, damage appeared to be due to straight-line winds.

A brief/weak tornado developed just west of Strasburg at 821 pm CDT on July 11 with minor tree damage observed near State Route 58.  The tornado moved into the village of Strasburg, damaging several trees from the southwest to northeast side of town.  Most of the tree limbs were six inches or less in diameter.  Some of the trees were snapped at their tops, particularly on the northeast side of town, where at least a dozen trees were noticeably snapped just south of a corn field just east of town.  The last sign of damage was observed on Struzick Road just northeast of Strasburg, where several small tree limbs were downed on a north-south stretch of the road south of 191st Street.  The tornado appears to have lasted approximately two minutes, with a path length less than a mile and a maximum width around 200 yards (though mostly much less narrower than this).

This quickly strengthening tornado developed southeast of Blue Grass and maintained 100 to 120 mph winds for much of its path into Davenport ending near Kimberly Rd. The most significant damage occurred at an RV sales business and adjacent residential neighborhood near I-280, as well as in and near Emeis Golf Course. Over 15 RVs were blown over, some blown 10 to 15 ft. The largest tipped over RV was 25,000 lbs. It was estimated over 80 moderate to large trees were snapped or uprooted along the path, in some places with high concentration. At least two unoccupied vehicles had trees fall on them.

This tornado intensified rapidly after development, and there was a visual from a farmstead to the north of the tornado developing. A dozen large trees at the first homestead hit were downed, some thrown, and heavy outbuilding, garage, and home roof damage. Further there were other homesteads/farmsteds that had outbuilding damage, utility poles downed (in one case thrown), and many trees snapped.
Brief tornado touchdown in a field. Location is approximate. Event time is based on radar data and EM report.
Brief tornado touchdown in a field. Location is approximate. Event time is based on radar data and EM report.

A 0.8 mile long EF1 tornado with peak wind speeds of 95 mph caused damage to trees and a county road maintenance shed in Bernard.  This tornado was surrounded by straight line wind damage with winds from 80 to 90 MPH.

Evidence of a multiple vortex tornado EF2 tornado occurred across northern Jackson County.  The tornado started north of La Motte where it damaged the roof of an agriculture industry building.  As it tracked east the tornado did damage to trees until halfway through its 2.6 mile path where the most intense damage was found.  A large farm building lost it's entire roof, along with half of it's walls.  Roof sheet metal was found north, south and east of the structure.  Insulation from the roof was found on the north, south and east side of the remaining walls.  A metal power pole was bent along with a few other wooden poles snap.  All this damage supported an EF2 tornado.  As the tornado moved east it destroyed two more farm buildings, numerous trees and the roof of a house.

EF1 tornado with peak winds of 105 mph hit a farm outbuilding around 320 PM.  The path continued through corn hitting a house, snapping some trees and destroying a garage at the end of its 0.7 mile long and 20 yd wide path.

This tornado developed just east of the Wapsipinicon River in Linn County and crossed into Jones County ending near U.S. Highway 151. Snapped large trees were found at a few locations, along with roof damage to a mobile home.
This tornado tracked through wooded areas of northeast Jones County. Significant tree damage occurred, including along the Maquoketa River such as in the Eby's Mill Wildlife Area.

EF1 tornado with a maximum wind of 95mph identified by satellite data and confirmed by aerial survey.  This tornado affected mainly crops across its 3.4 mile long path.  Towards the end of its path it destroyed a hoop building, removed a roof of a farm outbuilding and destroyed a garage at a residence.  A woman was trapped in the garage as it collapsed around her.
Fire-induced tornado
Video received showing brief touchdown in open field. A nearby home had some shingle damage.

Brief EF0 tornado with a 1.6 mile long track was identified from satellite data as well as pictures from Delaware County EMA.  The wall of a farm outbuilding was destroyed along with some tree damage. The path continued through some crops to the southeast.

Damage was mostly limited to shelter belt and wire fencing, however a primary home took minor damage to siding and had a glass door broken out.  EF0 was determined from the lack of damage to power lines that were directly in the path of the tornado.
The brief tornado crossed I-90 and was captured on video. Some corn and small tree branches were damaged.

Tornado started along Highway 78 near Racek Rd and went through the hills near the Black Hawk Unit before crossing County Highway Y, ending just across Highway 12.  The main area of damage was to the Birchwood Drive neighborhood where about 20 to 40 trees were uprooted or had multiple limbs broken off.  Multiple storm chaser videos show the main tornado tracking just west of this neighborhood.  The only structural damage noted that wasn't from falling trees was to one house on Birchwood Drive that had a few shingles pulled up.

Brief tornado that occurred in a field north of Beaver Dam west of Buckhorn Rd.  Reports from emergency management and storm chasers that there was a 15 to 20 second period where the rotation was in contact with the ground.  Damage was to the edge of a corn field and a tree that had a few tree branches knocked down.

An EF-1 rated tornado developed near the Farm and Fleet in Dodgeville, first moving northeast through a corn field.  The tornado then continued to the northeast, impacting numerous trees and one outbuilding.  The strongest damage occurred off of County Road ZZ, where numerous large, healthy hardwood trees were uprooted. The tornado ended near Knobs Road, just west of County Road H.

Tornado developed south of Hustisford near the intersection of Hillcrest Rd and County Rd E where a corn field had a convergent path going north-northeast through mainly farmland.  The tornado hit some trees south of Highway 60 and east of County Rd E before tracking north and going through near the intersection of Juneau St and Oakwood Blvd.  The tornado appears to have ended out over Sinissippi Lake.

An EF1 tornado impacted a home and adjacent homestead off of Grey Rd in far western Crook county. The tornado produced EF0 damage to several outbuildings south of the main single family residence. EF0 consisted of pushing and destroying a small shed outbuilding and pushing a storage silo off its pad and rotating it 45 degrees to the SW from its origin. The tornado tracked NE and continued to produce EF0 damage near the main home. Several trees near the home were snapped and the home loss some roofing material. The tornado continued to the NE before shifting to the ENE where it intensified to EF1. The tornado damaged a large outbuilding, ripping two concrete foots out of the ground and pushing the entire concrete brace from the foundation some 10 yards to the ENE. The entire structure had slid off the foundation with the structures walls all collapsed. The tornado then entered open field with no damage indicators available. A large debris field of tree branches and building material was thrown to the E, NE and N of the tornado track.
No damage reported. Track based on chaser video and reports.
This tornado tracked southeastward and damaged mainly corn along its track.

A brief tornado of unknown strength was confirmed using videos from social media, broadcast media, and local officials.  Based on this information combined with radar data, a very weak tornado occurred west of Patriot, Indiana in eastern Switzerland County.  

The tornadic circulation was fully condensed from the cloud base to the ground and exhibited sustained rotation. In addition to this, the depth of the rotation was tall enough within the thunderstorm, increasing confidence that this was not a landspout. The tornado was contained within heavily forested areas, limiting access for ground surveys. This resulted in no confirmed damage. While the tornado is being confirmed with unknown strength, the evidence from radar and the provided videos indicate the tornado was likely very weak and short lived. The exact location is approximated based on radar and geolocation techniques.  

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Switzerland County Indiana Emergency Management Agency for their assistance and coordination with this damage survey.

The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF1 tornado in Northridge in Clark County, Ohio.

The first evidence for this tornado was on the west side of Derr Road, where a tree was downed on a camper. Sporadic damage was noted in the next subdivision to the east, with some minor structural damage and numerous trees downed.

The most significant damage occurred north of Moorefield Road, along Ridgewood Road West, Waltin Lane, and Midland Road. Two homes had large portions of their roofs removed, with damage estimated to 100 MPH, within the EF1 category on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. One section of a roof was thrown across the road and into the backyard of another property. Additional debris was lofted and thrown into multiple trees. Shingle damage was noted on numerous homes, and tree damage was widespread through this neighborhood.

Damage to the east of Ridgewood Road East was more limited and sporadic, but several trees and large limbs were downed on Middle Urbana Road, Windy Ridge Drive, and Morris Road.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clark County Emergency Management Agency and officials with Moorefield Township for their assistance with this survey.

The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF0 tornado southeast of North Hampton in Clark County, Ohio.

The first evidence of this tornado occurred near Folk Ream Road, just south of Johnson Road. On Johnson Road. just to the east of Folk Ream Road, there were several downed tree branches and a few small snapped trees. On Shrine Road, north of Johnson Road, there was a significant amount of damage to corn on both sides of the road. Crop damage continued along the track of the tornado to the east-northeast, with damage to corn noted in several fields. The tornado is believed to have dissipated before reaching Ballentine Pike.

This statement was updated on July 23 to increase the length and width of the tornado, based on recent satellite imagery. The end time was also adjusted.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clark County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance.

Video evidence revealed the tornado began east of Sidney-Freyburg Road south of Wells Road and continued north. North of Wells Road, drone video revealed concentrated damage through the corn fields as it approached Lochard Road. Some minor tree damage was also observed near Lochard Road. Based on the drone video, the tornado is believed to have dissipated east of Lochard Road. 

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Shelby County Emergency Management Agency and the Shelby County Sheriff Office for their assistance with survey.

Sentinel-2 satellite imagery reveals high probability of tornado damage at this location within southeastern portions of Minnesota's Beltrami Island State Forest. Damage occurred in very rural and undeveloped area, with no reports of any damage to structures received. Damage indicators unknown at this time despite obvious damage to trees via satellite imagery. Time estimated via KMVX radar.

A tornado touched down west of Oconto at 6:00 PM CDT.  The tornado snapped and uprooted several trees before dissipating just north of Oconto at 6:04 PM CDT. The tornado uprooted several trees at a local golf course northwest of Oconto.

A tornado touched down in Gillett at 5:37 PM CDT.  The tornado tore the roof of a metal building, uplifted and damaged the roof of a nearby building, and snapped and uprooted several trees before dissipating east of Gillett at 5:40 PM CDT.

A tornado tracked for nearly four miles over approximately 21 minutes, leaving a path of significant damage.

The event began around 5:55 PM CDT when the tornado touched down in an open field between 168th and 169th Streets, just to the west of 442nd Avenue. The tornado initially tracked to the east, and by about 6:02 PM, it crossed 442nd Avenue.

The tornado then turned and started tracking south. The core of the tornado passed about 150 yards to the west of a farmstead, but at approximately 6:03 PM, the tornado was close enough to the farm to start causing significant damage. In fact, video evidence shows debris being lofted into the air before the tornado made its closest approach. The main residence was completely destroyed. An attached garage was dislodged and swept clean from its cement foundation; however, a vehicle in the driveway did not move. The remainder of the house lost its entire roof and many exterior walls, though many interior walls remained standing. One outbuilding was completely destroyed, and many others sustained significant damage. Along the southern edge of the property, a line of nine grain bins was completely swept away. The residents were not home at the time of the tornado, but a beloved horse was killed.

At 6:06 PM, the tornado crossed 169th Street and continued south through cropland. Aerial photos revealed that between 169th and 170th Streets, the tornado ripped through several rows of erosion shelterbelt trees. Trees in the path were void of branches, snapped at their bases, and in some spots, reduced to nothing more than stubs.

Continuing south, the tornado crossed 170th Street around 6:11 PM and continued across a lake and more cropland, eventually crossing 171st Street. By approximately 6:16 PM, the tornado weakened and dissipated just north of 172nd Street, bringing its 21-minute duration to an end.
Storm chaser video captured tornado move east of Dixon, SD with damage to trees, a farm outbuilding, and power poles.
Large tornado shown on storm chaser video, but across rough terrain with no roads. Track is based on known damage and Copernicus Sentinel data 2025.

The NWS Cleveland survey team, in coordination with the Wayne County Emergency Management Agency, conducted a storm damage assessment across northern Wayne County. They confirmed that an EF-0 tornado touched down along Fox Lake Road between Canaan Center Road and Route 3. The tornado caused minor damage to structures and trees, including a tree that was blown onto a mobile home and visible twisting of tree tops behind the house. As the tornado moved northeast, another tree was blown onto power lines east of Route 3, and several large limbs fell onto a car cover in the same area.

NWS Cleveland sincerely thanks Wayne County EMA for their support and collaboration during the survey process.
Quick spin-up within a broad swath of damaging winds. Damage consisted of a destroyed shed, destroyed barn and mangled trees at an abandoned farmstead, and a another destroyed large barn.
Attached are the only photos received from Custer County Sheriff's office. There are plenty of videos showing it on the ground.
Drone video shows track in open cornfield.
Track through mainly open fields with a few trees damaged along the way.

Numerous videos from social media show a weak tornado/funnel. Media shared images of tree and siding/roofing damage near the start of the tornado. Tornado path determined through use of satellite data. No injuries or fatalities reported. Start time based on radar estimate to be around 4:21 pm, end time based on end of satellite data to be around 4:25 pm.

...NWS Damage Survey for 07/31/25 Tornado Event...

.Overview...A waterspout formed over Spa Creek, passed briefly
as an EF0 tornado over the Severn Sailing Association marina at
the northernmost point of Eastport, Maryland, and then proceeded
back over the mouth of the Severn River as a waterspout.

.Eastport MD Tornado...

Rating:                 EF-0
Estimated Peak Wind:    65 mph
Path Length /statute/:  0.1 miles
Path Width /maximum/:   25 yards
Fatalities:             0
Injuries:               0

Start Date:             07/31/2025
Start Time:             2:46 PM EDT
Start Location:         Eastport MD / Anne Arundel County / MD
Start Lat/Lon:          38.975 / -76.481

End Date:               07/31/2025
End Time:               2:46 PM EDT
End Location:           Eastport MD / Anne Arundel County / MD
End Lat/Lon:            38.976 / -76.479

Survey Summary:
An individual at the Severn Sailing Association marina provided a
video of a waterspout between Eastport and the U.S. Naval Academy,
over Spa Creek. The waterspout moved into the shoreline at the
marina. That eyewitness saw the waterspout move ashore and over
the marina. They documented a few trailered and stored small boats
that were blown over by the wind in the parking area. The
circulation moved quickly back over water over the mouth of the
Severn River where additional social media video showed it as
viewed from near the Route 450 bridge. Terminal Doppler Weather
Radar TBWI operating nearby in northern Anne Arundel County showed
the circulation intensify briefly along this track, moving west to
east. It dissipated before reaching land on the other side of the
Severn River, and no other damage has been reported. The National
Weather Service would like to thank the Severn Sailing
Association, and the City of Annapolis Office of Emergency
Management for contributing to this survey.

A brief tornado occurred over northern rural Osceola County on Monday, August 4, 2025 as confirmed by a combination of video evidence from local media partners and data from the National Weather Service Melbourne (KMLB) radar. 

The tornado developed as a result of numerous low-level boundary collisions. The circulation is estimated to have touched down at approximately 7:14 PM EDT along the southern side of Lake Joel in St. Cloud, near Sungrove Ln and the C-32 Canal. KMLB radar data indicate the circulation, along with a corresponding debris signature, moved east over a densely wooded area before subsequently lifting around 7:22 PM EDT., just west of Storey Bend Rd. 

Given limited access to the affected area, the track is considered approximate, and an EF-rating cannot be provided at this time. Refinements to the track will be made if additional photographic or video evidence becomes available.
Radar TDS and ground survey suggests a brief rain wrapped tornado developed within the squall line. Will reassess the track when high resolution satellite data comes in.
This tornado likely rain wrapped intermittently produced damage across its nearly 4 mile long path with wind speeds up to 110mph.
intermittent path
Two videos confirm time and location of tornado. No damage was known with this brief tornado.
Brief touchdown confirmed by video. No damage was reported or known.
Video of a brief tornado touchdown. No damage reported or known.
Damage to corn

This tornado likely intermittent and rain wrapped destroyed 2 grain bins and produced shelterbelt tree damage along its nearly 3 mile long path with peak wind speeds estimated around 105mph.  Will reassess the track when high resolution satellite data comes in.

A brief tornado began just west of Madison Road/OH-528 just south of Burton-Windsor Road, roughly 3 miles northeast of Middlefield, OH. The tornado uprooted a large tree, with several large limbs snapped off trees in this area. The tornado continued to the northeast, crossing Madison Road, damaging three buildings on a property on the east side of the road. Two smaller outbuildings suffered extensive roof damage, with a larger barn suffering roof damage as well. Roofing material was thrown several hundred feet towards the west onto the roadway. Three livestock were reportedly injured.
Satellite data shows an EF-U tornado path through crops at this location.  This tornado did not hit any structures along its 2.2 mile long path.

This rain wrapped QLCS tornado produced some crop damage, seen via satellite, tipped over an irrigation pivot system and primarily  shelterbelt damage. Time estimated from KMVX radar with TDS observed.

The NWS survey team confirmed a tornado touched down in New London early Wednesday morning. The initial damage occurred at the New London Recreation Area near the small baseball field, where the storm blew over one of the bullpens. The tornado then tracked northeast, snapping a large hardwood tree in Grove Street Cemetery, with maximum wind speeds estimated at 90 mph. Several other large tree limbs in the cemetery were also broken.

Continuing into the residential area of New London, the tornado snapped and brought down several large tree tops and limbs, damaging two homes. Residents reported their ears popping and their homes shaking during the event. Further along its path, the tornado uprooted a large hardwood tree and landed it on a home. The home suffered roof damage from the fallen tree. Another uprooted tree fell onto power lines, snapping three utility poles and blocking the roadway. Before dissipating, the tornado also knocked down several panel fences.

The NWS appreciates the New London Fire Department and Huron County EMA for their help during the storm survey.

This QLCS tornado was likely rain wrapped with the starting location approximated based on high resolution satellite imagery with scouring occurring in a wheat field. The tornado moved to the northeast and encountered the 120 ft by 60 ft pole barn. The barn was completely destroyed.

A waterspout associated with a tornadic thunderstorm over water moved onshore near the 1200 block of Ocean Blvd W. Minor damage was noted to several palm trees, and numerous pieces of beach furniture were tossed around before the tornado dissipated over the dune line.

Video and picture evidence showed a funnel cloud developing north of Homer. Sentinel satellite data suggested a brief touchdown in a corn field about 1.5 miles east of the Vermilion/Champaign County line and north of Catlin-Homer Rd.
Satellite imagery reveals likely tornado damage seen within crops. Large tree branches snapped. Time estimated from KMVX radar. TDS observed on radar.

Mostly tree and crop damage. Most trees were large cottonwood trees uprooted and snapped half way up the trunk. Time estimated from KVX radar. TDS observed on radar. Sentinel-2 imagery reveals crop damage.

Garage door of large shed torn off at farmstead with numerous large branches down across property as well as tree uprooted. Numerous large tree branches snapped and uprooted along path. Time estimated from KVX radar. TDS observed on radar. Sentinel-2 imagery reveals crop damage.

A tornado briefly touched down south of Clintonville at 5:32 PM CDT, moving east-northeast before dissipating at 5:34 PM CDT. The tornado was spotted by the local fire department and tracked over mainly open areas with little to no damage indicators. The only damage indicators were disturbances to crops on satellite analysis. Path estimated based on radar and satellite imagery. No injuries or fatalities reported.

An EF-0 tornado touched down on Sinking Cove Road causing several uprooted trees. It briefly tracked south southeastward uprooting additional trees, passing across Little Crow Creek before lifting just west of The Bolo Club on Sinking Cove Road where no additional tree damage was noted. Damage was assessed via drone footage taken by Jackson County Emergency Management in coordination with Franklin County (TN) Emergency Management. Supplemental satellite imagery is being ordered to assess damage for inaccessible areas, and subsequent track modifications may occur to the start and end point. Thank you to Jackson County, AL and Franklin County, TN EMA for their coordination.
Satellite imagery reveals likely tornado damage seen within crops. Time estimated from KMVX radar.

This QLCS tornado was very brief with damage confined to one field. The sunflowers were flattened in a very short concentric and convergent path. Time estimated from KMVX radar. TDS observed on radar.

This QLCS tornado was very brief with damage confined to one field and shelterbelt. The sunflowers were flattened in a very short concentric and convergent path. Time estimated from KMVX radar. TDS observed on radar.

This slow moving tornado started in a marshy low lying field and tracked east then northeast encountering a grove of trees. Here the tornado snapped off many tree trunks and continued to the northeast with scouring occurring in the corn field. It encountered another grove of trees snapping more large branches and tree trunks before lifting near 101st Street SE.
Sentinel satellite imagery revealed a track in agricultural fields. No DI's were impacted resulting in an EF-U rating.
Sentinel satellite imagery revealed a track in agricultural fields, just missing a farmstead. No DI's were impacted resulting in an EF-U rating.

Door County Emergency Management supported damage survey with photos and on-site analysis. NWS Green Bay confirmed tornado path of convergent damage pattern, radar analysis, environmental analysis, and satellite imagery. 

Damage was consistent with EF-0 tornado, with most significant damage being an uprooted tree. NWS went to low end of damage scale, as ground was saturated. 

Tornado cross into Eagle Harbor as a waterspout. Numerous public reports of waterspout, along with video. 

No injuries or fatalities reported
Very brief EFU tornado based on storm chaser video footage.  Looked to be multiple vortex in nature.

Based on a thorough review of damage reports and radar data, the NWS in State College has confirmed an EF-0 tornado occurred on Thursday evening September 4th. The brief tornado spun up southeast of Collins, PA and lifted the roof off of a dugout at Solanco Youth Baseball Association at 9:31PM. The tornado continued across Kirkwood Pike and caused crop damage in a field just north of Encounter Church. The tornado lifted before it encountered a wooded residential area northwest of Hideaway Drive.

We would like to thank several students and alumni of the Millersville Meteorology program and meteorologists at WGAL for their assistance with relaying reports and sharing photos from the event.
This short lived tornado damaged crops, a barn, and a tree stand. A pronounced track in fields noted via satellite and UAV photos and a TDS noted on radar.
EF-Unknown. Identified from EMA provided drone overflight and confirmed in Sentinel Satellite Imagery.

Tornado briefly touched down near Arrowhead drive in Paxton, crossing Richards Ave and likely lifting after causing significant tree damage in its path. Several softwood trees snapped at the trunk or uprooted.
Tornado briefly touched down near a section of South road and Paxton. Damage was limited to several softwood trees being uprooted.
EF1 tornado briefly touched down over Will Brook Rd in Holden.

EF1 tornado touched down west of Barnes Hill road in Berlin, MA and traveled ENE crossing Derby road and West street. Many soft or hardwood trees snapped at the trunk or uprooted. Survey was conducted using drone footage supplied by Berlin, Police Department. Special thanks to  their team for their assistance.

An EF1 tornado touchdown down in Stow, MA near Maple street and continued ENE over Bose Avenue causing significant tree damage. The tornado lifted somewhere near Harvest Drive and touched down again about 1.25 miles ENEjust west of Pacakard road and continued across Carriage lane before lifting again. This tornado caused significant tree damage with several hard and softwood trees uprooted or snapped at the trunk.

A microburst produced a narrow swath of wind damage in the town of Gillham, AR from just south of the Kansas City Southern Railway to just east of US Hwy 71. The damage consisted almost entirely of uprooted hardwood and softwood trees, although a few softwood trees were also snapped. The damage was particularly concentrated just north of and down a hill from the Gillham Baptist Church. The damage pattern was almost entirely unidirectional, pointing to the northeast, and even diverged slightly in a couple of places, which strongly indicated this was straight-line wind damage. A UAS overflight by was conducted by local officials. The survey team did not see the video, but local officials confirmed the unidirectional damage path. The tree damage was consistent with straight-line winds near 90 mph.

Many thanks go to the Sevier County Office of Emergency Management for their assistance in mapping damage and for conducting the UAS overflight.
Satellite confirmed tornado track. Video confirmed branches down at a farmstead.

A tornado briefly touched down north of Northland at 5:04 PM CDT,
moving east-northeast before turning east-southeast and then
dissipating at 5:13 PM CDT.  The tornado snapped and uprooted a
few trees and produced minor damage to a house. Based on
satellite analysis, there may have been a few brief moments where
the tornado lifted off the ground before dissipating west of Big
Falls.

The first signs of tornado damage were documented at a farm roughly six miles southeast of Mobridge along SD Highway 1804, where a grain silo sustained minor damage. About half a mile to the northwest along the same highway, a semi-trailer was tipped over, with a second semi-trailer overturned another mile beyond that.

Continuing northwest on SD Highway 1804, the tornado destroyed an entire outbuilding on a farm located about one mile south of US Highway 12. The roof was ripped from the building and its eastern walls collapsed. 

The tornado then tracked northwest and approached  US Highway 12. It was at this point that storm chasers documented the tornado, although heavy precipitation often obscured their view. Along this highway, one power pole was bent and a camper being pulled by a vehicle was overturned. Thankfully, no injuries were reported.

After crossing US Highway 12, the tornado tracked just west of 290th Avenue, taking down a series of six power poles that were either completely broken or severely bent. This was likely the widest point of the tornado. No other damage was noted beyond this location, however information remains preliminary as more photos and satellite imagery are analyzed in the coming days.
Storm chasers reported a brief tornado touchdown over open land, roughly 8 miles northeast of Wakpala, SD. No damage was reported.
EF-Unknown. Identified from EMA provided drone overflight and confirmed in Sentinel Satellite Imagery.
Brief touchdown in an open field.
Eyewitnesses sent photo and video of a tornado over the Missouri River. The tornado never touched land.

NWS Bismarck received report of a barn destroyed near the intersection of Highway 1804 and Highway 13, near Beaver Bay. A survey team was dispatched and found grass and crop damage on a road south of the farm property. This was the likely start of the tornado. The tornado then travelled northwest where it dented in the south facing side of a large, and mostly empty, grain bin. It then proceeded to destroy an 80 by 124 foot pole barn to the north. On this barn, a small wall where a side garage door remained standing. Inside the barn, farm equipment was damaged. The south facing door to this barn was resting on a combine tractor. Debris was scattered in all directions and several hundred feet away. Large pieces of board from the destroyed building were embedded in the ground including part of a rafter. There was limited tree damage to the row of trees to the north of this property. No one was home at the time, thus no injuries. Storm chasers noted this tornado progressed north before roping out.

Storm chaser reported seeing a tornado begin southeast of Wilton around 4:09 PM. NWS Storm survey team found a twisted piece of metal in a ditch east of Wilton. There was also flattened grass nearby this debris. In a field to the south of this debris was a potential tornado track, although it could not be confirmed as perhaps it could have been a drainage channel from heavy rains. Time of tornado near debris was estimated.
Storm chasers report tornado near Arena. Towards the end of this track, storm chasers report multiple vortex tornado. No damage was reported.

Updated path to have two tornadoes near Mercer. This longer lived tornado was responsible for damage near and north of Mercer. NWS Survey Team found damage at a farm just west of Mercer. Occupants were home at the time, and noted a lack of a loud roar like in a previous tornado. The tornado brought lots of tree damage to the property with many branches and trees snapped, and a large tree uprooted. From there the tornado partially destroyed a pole barn. Half of the rafters were ripped off. Debris was scattered all over and up to a quarter mile away. Large pieces of wood were embedded in the ground in the debris field. On the southeast side of the building, several large support beams buried about 5 deep were pulled out. From there the tornado crossed Highway 200, damaging trees on the north side of the highway. It then proceeded north and destroyed an unanchored and unoccupied mobile home on wheels being stored north of Mercer. This same property had a security camera video of the tornado. Radar may have shown a debris ball at about the time of this damage. The tornado then ended shortly north of this mobile home damage as reported by storm chasers.

At around 5:59 PM CDT storm chasers reported a large wedge tornado beginning several miles south of Butte. Storm chasers tracked this tornado north to just west then north of Butte. At around 6:11 PM storm chasers stopped in Butte for gas and recorded the outer edge of the tornado moved over them. Some debris was seen blown in this video. No other damage was reported with this tornado. Tornado was reported to end north of Butte around 6:14 PM CDT.

Updated path to start west of Highway 14 near the need of the first Denhoff satellite tornado. NWS received damage reports near Denhoff. A survey team was sent to assess and here are their findings. When the tornado reached about 6 miles south of Denhoff, it destroyed a 30 by 60 foot pole barn. A nearby barn had 2 skylights torn off the roof. Another nearby building had some minor damage. At this same property, a double wide mobile home propped up on a basement had the roof completely torn off and blown to the west side of the home. The southeast corner of this mobile home was also missing a wall. A car parked some distance was picked up and set down near the mobile home. Debris was scattered everywhere at this property and there was also a lot of tree damage, mostly snapped branches. The tornado then continued north. About a mile south of Denhoff a single wide mobile home was flipped. There was also debris scattered up to a quarter mile away near this property. Noticeable tree damage as well. Some haybales also reported damaged. The tornado then continued west and north of Denhoff. Near a gravel pit there was more haybale and tree damage. Several other properties then experience damage from 2 to 5 miles north of Denhoff. There was haybale damage and hay embedded in a road sign’s wood post north of Denhoff. Roof panels were missing from a farm outbuilding north of this road sign. North of this, another property had missing skylights on a farm building, damage to a small grain bin, and a kids wooden play area destroyed. Multiple areas of tree damage were also seen north of Denhoff by NWS Survey Team. The tornado was then estimated to end 5 to 6 miles north of Denhoff. No injuries reported. Of note, chasers and those NWS Survey Team talked to mentioned multiple times of a second tornado near the main one. This tornado at one point crossed a lake and pulled up water. If confirmed this would be counted as a separate tornado with a near parallel path.
Short-lived satellite tornado north of the multivortex Denhoff tornado that has a preliminary EF-2 rating. Time, duration, and location are based off of storm chaser footage.

Updated path as storm chaser reports intermittent rope tornado to the south of the Denhoff multivortex tornado that has a preliminary rating of EF-2. Time, duration, and estimated location from storm chaser footage. Some comments from footage on corn crops damaged but have no other confirmation. Footage also those this tornado crossing Highway 14 from east to west then passing over a water source and ingesting water into funnel.
Videos from storm chasers and locals show a tornado that developed northwest of Wing near Haystack Butte. Path is estimated and tornado was likely intermittent along the path.

Storm chaser confirmed tornado correlates with strong radar signature. End time is estimated, as tornado was somewhat rain wrapped and hard to see. Minor tree damage mentioned on storm chaser footage but no confirmation of that at this time.

A tornado touched down over cropland just east of 439th Ave and about a half-mile south of 183rd St. The tornado tracked northeast, crossing 183rd Street. Tree damage was noted just before the tornado crossed 440th Ave. The tornado then approached a farm on 182nd St, where several empty grain bins were detached from their foundations and destroyed. The last evidence of the tornado was in a crop field roughly a half-mile north of this farm, or three-quarters of a mile east-southeast of Hazel.
Trained weather spotter reported brief tornado just south of Granville.

As storms formed along a weak boundary, a weak but highly visible tornado developed in a farm field. The tornado remained in fields as it drifted southeastward. It caused no structural damage, but did some very minor tree damage. The tornado crossed Hwy 10 and dissipated in a field.
Storm chaser reports new large multi vortex tornado 8 to 10 miles southeast of Kief. Reports tornado diminished a short time after 5:29 PM. No damage reported. Track estimated based on radar.

Storm chasers report intermittent tornado touchdown from around Balfour to near Karlsruhe. Tornado became rain wrapped and hard to observe later on in the track. Radar data was used to estimate the end point of this tornado. No Damage was reported.
Storm chaser reports tornado southeast of Fort Yates. Location estimated based on radar. No damage reported.

Storm chaser reports and shared video of a tornado forming north or Driscoll the tracking north northwest. The tornado crosses 405th St NE just north of a farmstead. It then continues northward and likely crossed 110th Ave NE and diminishes near a body of water. Near the end of the tornado storm chaser reports crop damage, which was also reported by broadcast media. No other damage was reported with this tornado.

Storm chaser reports and shared video of tornado briefly touching down southeast of Mercer. Reports and video showed tornado diminished before new longer tracked tornado began west of Mercer. No damage reported with this initial tornado.

Storm chasers reported a tornado west of Karlsruhe. This tornado moved north northwest before lifting northwest of Karlsruhe. No damage was reported with this tornado, however, radar showed CC drop on a couple of scans. Track estimated based on reports and radar.
Storm chasers report another brief tornado north of Karlsruhe. Radar showed a drop in CC at 6:59 PM CDT. No damage was reported. Tornado track estimated based on radar and storm chaser reports.

The tornado began in a corn field northwest of Mount Sterling with drone footage capturing the swirling corn pattern. The tornado continued southeast damaging a farm outbuilding and several buildings in town before dissipating.

A narrow path of downed crops was visible from Copernicus Sentinel data 2025 and confirmed from Lincoln County Sheriff drone photos. Some minor tree damage was observed at a farmstead along 469th Ave between 289th St and 288th St, resulting in a EF0 rating.

Storm chaser video confirmed tornado started approximately 2 miles east of Menoken. The tornado was probably intermittently on the ground, traveling northwest before coming to a farmstead just north of Interstate 94. This is where the most significant damage occurred, with the tin roof of an old pole barn ripped off and tossed into nearby trees. The damage to the pole barn was given an EF-1 damage rating. Various debris was scattered across the property, including a trampoline, and a larger barn door was dented. The tornado then progressed further to the northwest, crossing 158th Street Northeast and impacting another property. At this location, a single-wide trailer had shingle damage and a few 75 year old trees had either large branches down or were fully uprooted. Estimated max wind with this tornado was 95 mph.

A weak tornado touched down four miles southeast of the Aberdeen Regional Airport. It blew apart a swing set and launched a trampoline into a nearby cornfield. Spotty damage to the corn crop was also noted.

An NWS storm survey crew confirmed a path of sporadic and very inconsistent straight-line wind damage in Howard County, AR, between Milford and Nashville. The damage began northeast of Milford, north and west of Longview Road, where some large limbs were downed and one large hardwood tree was snapped. More uprooted trees were noted along Rock Creek to the west. There was a large break in the path before more damage was noted, beginning along AR Hwy 355 between Cassady Lane and Mission Drive. Several sheds and outbuildings suffered partial or complete removal of their metal roofs, and several trees were uprooted, with the occasional snap being observed. Several cypress trees were snapped at a hog farm north of Mission Drive. Directly south of Mission Drive, a chicken house lost several metal roof panels. More trees sustained large limb damage or were uprooted along Garner Loop and Waterloo Road. Additional trees were also along Feemster Road.

As mentioned, the damage was very sporadic and inconsistent. A convergent damage pattern could not be found. If anything, damage patterns were unidirectional or divergent to the southeast, south, or southwest. This suggests damage was likely caused by straight-line winds associated with the forward-flank downdraft (FFD) and/or the rear-flank downdraft (RFD) of the supercell. Damage on Feemster Road was clearly caused by the FFD and pointed north. Drone video provided by the Howard County Office of Emergency Management also showed similar observations. Maximum wind gusts were estimated to be 90-95 mph.

Many thanks go to the Howard County Office of Emergency Management for their assistance in locating the damage, providing initial photos and assessments, and for their drone overflight.

Just before noon, a storm along a warm front separated from the rest of the line and began to rotate. With a favorable environment but low instability, a weak tornado touched down near Callicoon Center. The damage in town was mostly branches down but given that its where the circulation strengthened, its likely that the winds that knocked down the branches were associated with a weak tornado. Up the hill on J Young RD there was a greater amount of Damage observed, with the tornado crossing paths with old tornado damage from April 22, 2023. No damage was observed on Huber Rd and down towards Hazel so its likely the circulation became disorganized and remained aloft. Continuing along Beaver Hill Rd, there was more damage along the path of rotation that had a cyclonic pattern to the trees that fell on each side of the road. With near peak fall foliage, it is likely that the leaves were being lofted more easily than normal leading to the debris signature on radar despite how weak the tornado was.

Around 12:36 PM CDT on September 24, 2025, a brief EF-1 tornado touched down in south Benton, near the Lost River Estates development. The tornado initially blew down a fence in the backyard of a residential home on the south side of the development. It also snapped a softwood tree across Palmetto Road. The tornado then crossed the road where it snapped large tree branches at the entrance of the Bossier Parish Schools Maintenance Palmetto Warehouse. Aside from ripping a road sign out of the ground on the west side of Palmetto Road, the tornado also damaged a residential entrance on the east side of the road. At the same time, a trash can from the Lost River Estates was spotted in the open field on the north side of the warehouse suggesting strong winds. The tornado then lifted abruptly, as no damage was detected at the warehouse or the adjacent barns and homes along Duval Street and James Street access road.
Virtual damage assessment was done, using satellite imagery and images received from Saguache County Emergency Manager.

Media relayed a video of a landspout tornado viewed from SE edge of Fairmount looking SE towards Jamaica. The specific location was estimated based on report details. Witness reported that they watched it form and dissipate, and a second formed in the same area within a few minutes. Video shows the base of the landspout over open fields.

An EF-1 tornado touched down on the northwest side of the Hammond Northshore Regional Airport just before 4am CDT where patches of large branches were snapped. The tornado continued to the north-northwest across highways 443 and 1064 where it maintained EF-0 strength by snapping small branches. The tornado remained over rural parts of northern Hammond while steadily picking up strength. The tornado was nearing peak intensity as it approached the intersection of Faller Rd and Tycer Ln at 4:06am where a house lost an awning and parts of its roof. The tornado finally reach peak intensity at as it continued to the north-northwest and approaches the intersection of Faller Rd and McManus Dr. Here, a hardwood tree was snapped in the middle. The tornado maintained this peak intensity as it approached Highway 442 where a few more hardwood trees were snapped. The tornado began weakening after this point as is continued to make its way to the north-northwest and across the Tangipahoa River. As it crossed the river, it practically paralleled S Bennett Rd in Independence, LA where it mainly snapped large branches until it lifted shortly before Highway 40 at 4:14am.

An EF-1 touched down south of Robert, LA at 5:11am CDT along Traino Rd where a few small limbs were snapped. The tornado quickly gained strength as it moved north towards Highway 22. The tornado reached peak intensity as a 90mph EF-1 at 5:14am along Highway 20 just east of the Fairhope Subdivision where a group of softwood trees were snapped. This tornado maintained peak intensity as it continued northward towards Crown Dr at 5:18am. Here more softwood trees were snapped and a roof was partially removed from a manufactured home. The tornado began to weaken and occlude as it moved to the northeast. The tornado broke small limbs and caused small trees to lean in a convergent pattern before lifting at 5:21am just southwest of Jasper Ln south of Robert, LA.

A brief EF-0 touched down just north of Highway 445 on Bailey Loop Rd in Loranger, LA at 4:57am CDT where it broke off patches of large branches. This tornado continued due northward into forested areas of Loranger before making it to Bradford Ln at 5:04am. Here, more patches of small and large branches were broken before the tornado lifted along Highway 40 still at 5:04am.

Minor vegetation damage was identified using high resolution satellite imagery to verify the track of a radar-confirmed EF-0 tornado that occurred near Blind River, southeast of Denson, LA in Livingston Parish. This weak tornado remained away from any structures though a weak, but conclusive tornado debris signature was visible on KHDC radar imagery which aligned with intermittent minor vegetation over the marsh. Most notably a few trees were visibly displaced on the bank of Blind River.

This brief QLCS tornado started near Sycamore Drive in Hot Spring County, just north of highway 128, and produced mainly tree damage along a short path. The tornado moved eastward, and dissipated as it reached Owasso Trail. Survey results found damage consistent with an EF1 tornado.
The tornado touched down in an open field south of Zap and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF-U (Unknown).

A narrow, brief tornado touched down along Eagle Bend Road south of Yazoo City where the top of a Pecan tree was downed onto a home. Fortunately, the home sustained limited if any damage. The tornado continued to move northeast, paralleling Eagle Bend Road while staying slightly north of the roadway. Intermittent vegetative damage was noted with a isolated tree fall as well. The tornado remained at EF-0 intensity through its duration before dissipating near Old Highway 3 where minor roofing tin peeling was noted. The tornado's maximum winds were estimated at 85 mph, EF-0. It's maximum width was around 50 yards with a track length of just over 3 miles (3.03).

Working with Jessamine County EMA on a survey, the National Weather Service in Louisville found a tornado occurred on Sunday October 19th in west Nicholasville at the RJ Corman Group complex near Highway 27.  The tornado is believed to have started off as a cold air funnel that was able to briefly get down to the surface.  The tornado touched down at Big Tunnel Road near Jessamine Creek with uprooted trees and large branch damage.  From the damage, there was a convergent signature that is consistent with a tornadic circulation.  The tornado moved across a field and more tree damage was observed near RJ Corman Drive.  The tornado then hit an RJ Corman warehouse where a garage door was blown out and a portion of the warehouse wall was pulled away from the building. Security camera footage confirms that a very small funnel caused the damage to the building.  Pieces of insulation, wood planks, and metal from the walls of the building were lifted to the rooftop.  On the roof of the building, a few HVAC units were displaced from their locations.  The maximum sustained winds were 90 mph at the metal building.  The tornado continued across a paved lot and ended shortly after RJ Corman Drive to the west of US Highway 27 for a total distance of 0.65 miles.

The National Weather Service would like to extend a big thank you to Jessamine County Emergency Management for assisting with surveying the damage and providing pictures and drone footage, as well as to the RJ Corman Group for providing security camera footage of the tornado.

A brief tornado touched down along Shell Oil Rd in southeast Brandon and traveled southeast for 6.7 miles before lifting near Gill Rd in Johns. The tornado was on the ground for roughly 10 minutes. Numerous large and small tree branches were downed along the path.

An EF-1 tornado touched down just south of the Hunters Bend area and moved northeast through the community. Several large trees were blown down across power lines and Hunters Bend Road near the start, with continued tree damage through the forest areas to the northeast. Trees were snapped and uprooted where the road turned north. Additional damage to a mobile home and several barns and outbuildings occurred at the east of of Dr. Thomason Road at the Tensas River. A 12x24 foot hunting shed was completely destroyed with debris blown north into the tree line. High resolution satellite imagery and accounts from area landowners indicated that the tornado continued east across Tensas River bend into National Wildlife Refuge land with damage at least 200 yards wide in that area. The tornado ended in a field south of Sharky Rd.
Several points along creek have twisted trees and structural damage. GRK shows velocity couplet supporting rotation and tornadic wind damage.

An EF-0 tornado touched down near the intersection of Palermo Drive and Evangeline Street in Sulphur. The tornado then tracked across McMurry Park and into the Maplewood
Neighborhood. Several homes in the area sustained minor damage, including damage to roofs, awnings, and fences. There was also tree damage, and a few power lines were pulled from their poles.  The tornado continued over Lowe`s before crossing I-10 and dissipating near the intersection of Pete Manena Road and Bayou D`Inde Road. Tree damage was also observed along I-10 where the tornado crossed the interstate.

The tornado touched down near Arlington Elementary School and moved northeastward causing generally minor damage to trees and a few residential roofs. The tornado was strongest as it approached Old Mobile Ave, where it uprooted several trees in a convergent pattern on the south side of the road near the intersection with Chateau Dr. As the tornado approached the north side of the Briarwood subdivision along Arrowhead Dr, it began to occlude, taking turn to the north and then northwest as it approached Industrial Ave. It then crossed Hwy 90 and lifted as it approached Shortcut Rd.

The tornado touched down just south of the intersection of Kleinschmidt Road and County Road 87, where minor tree damage was observed. Traveling to the northeast, the tornado crossed County Road 87, uprooting a couple of trees and removing portions of the roof from a small barn. The tornado continued to the northeast before strengthening along Woerner Road South. Here, a large barn lost much of its metal roof paneling, and several trees were uprooted. The tornado appears to have lifted before crossing Woerner Road.

October 29th update: Additional drone video was provided along County Road 87 that revealed the path width being close to 125 yards and an additional patch of trees within a tree stand behind the ground surveyed properties that had several skinny pine trees snapped low bringing the intensity to 95mph.

Special thanks to the Baldwin County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

After review of available high-resolution satellite imagery, the tornado was found to have begun slightly earlier in the forest to the south of Kleinschmidt Road. The tornado was also found to have turned to the east as it crossed Woerner Road South where it did minor tree damage before lifting.

A tornadic waterspout moved onshore into Mexico Beach at approximately 630am CT, causing roof and siding damage to a couple of homes along the beach. The roof of the El Governor hotel was lifted and tossed across U.S. 98 into an RV park, where several RV's were damaged or rolled over. A number of minor injuries were reported at the RV park. The tornado continued eastward, moving inland across several neighborhoods. Roof damage, the most significant of which involved the peeling of metal roofing, was noted at several locations. Otherwise, the damage was scattered and mostly minor. The tornado dissipated before reaching Highway 386. The damage was consistent was an EF-1 tornado with maximum winds of approximately 100 mph.

A very brief tornado tracked across U.S. Highway 98, damaging fencing and signs in a new construction neighborhood. The fencing was blown from east to west across the highway. No structural damage was noted and the damage appeared consistent with an EF-0 tornado with maximum winds of approximately 70 mph.

This EF1 tornado developed from a weak, shallow supercell northeast of Lindale. The tornado began along CR 4114 northeast of Macs Creek Lake, breaking large tree limbs. It moved east, crossing FM 1804/Hoard Road, where it caused a significant loss of shingles from a single-family residence. The tornado moved east-southeast through a wooded area and broke more large tree limbs as it crossed CR 452. A double-wide manufactured home also sustained some minor roof damage.

The tornado intensified and damage became more concentrated as it crossed CR 4129 and CR 4106. Several trees were snapped and uprooted in this area. At the intersection of CR 4106 and CR 4128, a single-family residence suffered significant loss of shingles and the collapse of the brick facade on the east side of the home. However, the wooden walls and frame remained solidly standing. Just south of the intersection of CR 4126 and CR 4128, numerous pine trees were snapped, and a couple of large hardwood trees were uprooted. One house on the farm sustained major damage to its roof. An outbuilding lost most of its metal roof panels, and those that remained attached to the wooden frame showed significant twisting. The family on the farm told the survey team that they witnessed one of their flatbed trailers be lofted into the air above treetop level when the tornado struck.

The tornado turned southeast and removed half the roof from a wood-and-metal home. A couple of hardwood trees were also uprooted on this property. The tornado continued southeast, snapped a couple more pine trees, and caused some minor shingle damage to a single-family home along CR 4104 before lifting.

Many thanks go to the Smith County Office of Emergency Management and the Texas Department of Emergency Management for their assistance in locating the damage.

This EF1 tornado began along CR 1122 in Gregg County, just east of FM 2012, west of Kilgore. A few trees were snapped and uprooted. A double-wide manufactured home lost most of its metal skirting and sustained the loss of about half of its roof and porch covering. The tornado continued east and caused significant roof damage to a second double-wide manufactured home. As the tornado entered the city of Kilgore, two businesses along Industrial Blvd lost most of their roofs.

As the tornado reached Commerce Street at Harris Street Park, most of the damage consisted of snapped and uprooted trees from this point forward. Dugouts were damaged at Driller Park. The tornado turned southeast, crossed into Rusk County, and entered a residential area beginning at Florence Street and Monroe Street. Most of the damage consisted of snapped and uprooted trees, which damaged a few homes. Other homes sustained minor shingle loss. The tornado generally followed Monroe Street while crossing Martin, South, and Simmons Streets before lifting near the intersection of Hunter Street and Broadway Blvd.

Many thanks go to the City of Kilgore Office of Emergency Management for their assistance in this damage survey.

An EF-0 tornado crossed Bear Island Road south of Hwy 22, causing damage mostly to trees. One home suffered minor roof damage, and a large metal canopy was thrown about 25 to 40 yard to the southeast. High resolution satellite imagery helped to identify the start and end of this tornado over the inaccessible marsh areas where defoliation and minor tree damage were evident. The marsh damage was also collocated with an evident tornado debris signature on KHDC radar imagery.

An EF-1 tornado was confirmed by NWS ground survey northeast of Hammond, LA in Tangipahoa Parish. The ground survey first noted damage near River Rd and Arbuthnott Drive. The tornado moved generlaly northward to the east of River Rd causing additional damage mostly to trees. The strongest damage surveyed was along Dummyline Rd where it snapped several large trees, before the tornado crossed the Tangipahoa River. It then caused additional tree damage and destroyed a tent on the grounds of Camp Living Waters. Remote survey techniques utilizing high-resolution satellite imagery identified additional damage just north of Dusty Ln between Diana Ln and Calmes Ln, as a start point. The same imagery also indicated the tornado continued past the cap ground, causing tree damage near Robert Perkins Rd, and gradually weakening and lifting as it approached Chappepeela Rd.
Damage path was not continuous. Straight-line wind damage was also observed north and south of the tornado path.

The damage path of an EF-1 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery over inaccessible rural marsh areas of Terrebonne Parish, southwest of Humphreys, LA. This tornado began southwest of Blue Bird Canal where a defined, but weak path of damage to marsh vegetation was evident. The marsh damage continued northeast across Blue Bird Canal, narrowly missing fishing camps, and was collocated with a strong tornado vortex signature on KHDC radar imagery. The tornado intensified as it crossed the Intracoastal Waterway and Lake Hackberry with numerous displaced trees evident along a canal and maximum path width around 250 yards. This was collocated with a tornado debris signature that was identified on Climavision V014 radar imagery. The tornado continued northeast and quickly weakened which is corroborated by KHDC and Climavision radar imagery. The tornado evidently lifted prior to reaching structures along Bayou Black Drive in Humphreys.
A video from a trained spotter verified a brief landspout tornado over a farm field south of MN60 east of Kenyon. No damage was observed. Location and time approximate based on radar and video.
Estimated path of EF-U tornado.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey Team has determined that the damage that occurred near Bland Point, VA during the evening of Sunday, November 9 is consistent with that from an EF0 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 85 mph and a maximum width around 50 yards. A severe storm tracked from WSW to ENE across the Piankatank River during the evening of November 9, 2025. While the storm had bowed out prior to crossing the river, a velocity enhancement developed along the apex of the bow while it was over the waters. This surge likely aided in the formation of a waterspout over the Piankatank River which crossed over the shoreline as a tornado in the Bland Point section of Deltaville. The tornado touched down around 935 PM EST along the western shore of Bland Point, causing mainly tree top damage. The worst damage from the first house was a large oak tree which fell northeast towards the house, landing in the pool and causing damage to the pool and pool furniture. However, this tree had significant rot inside of it which may have made it easier to fall compared to nearby trees. While the tree was facing northeast, several large branches were in the Piankatank River, southwest of nearby trees. As the tornado moved almost due east, it twisted and snapped three trees near each other with two trees facing east while the other faced northeast. A large branch from a pine tree was blown roughly 12 yards from the tree. Some of the pine tree branches were blown into a nearby house, breaking two large windows and a wooden window frame. The wind was strong enough to embed small pine twigs and branches into the stucco siding of the house. Additionally, a picnic table at this property was broken into pieces and thrown roughly 20 to 30 feet. A patchy of shingles was damaged from a garage attached to a third house at the apex of Bland Point. At this location, a sliding glass door frame, that was rated to withstand category 1 hurricanes, was pushed inward. Additionally, furniture on the second story balcony was pushed hard enough to bend and partially dislodge the metal railing. Just outside of the house, 20 heavy duty pool chairs, some made out of polywood and some made out of aluminum, were lofted and thrown around 40 yards. Most of the chairs were broken or shattered. Debris from the pool furniture was thrown hard enough to dent the bark of a bush more than 50 yards from the pool. At this point, it appeared that the tornado turned to the northeast, following the shoreline. A few wicker pool chairs were damaged at another house with a couple of large bushes uprooted another property to the northeast. At this final house, the winds were strong enough to rip a large metal sheet attached to an in-ground pool cover off of the pool and throw it into 2000 pound marble pillars nearby with enough force to both bend the metal at nearly a 90 degree angle and to knock over a couple pillars. To the southeast of the pillars, several wooden planks were blown off of a wooden dock. The tornado then tracked likely along or just offshore of the shoreline for around 220 yards before dissipating around 936 PM EST. Several trees were twisted and snapped in the woods, landing in a variety of directions, with the majority facing southeast.

This tornado was documented by local residents. It occurred in the location south of Loop 143 and north of County Road L, between County Road 15 and US Highway 83. It was on the ground briefly with no known damage associated with it.

Evidence of the tornado began on Highway 94 just east of Hickman. A very narrow tornado then slowly moved southeast, mostly across open fields, doing sporadic minor tree damage before snapping 3 power poles along and near Highway 166 ending near Rice Lane and Highway 166. Photos from the event show a very narrow funnel consistent with the narrow damage path.

The tornado began north of Guthrie where several trees were snapped. The narrow tornado moved east across open fields where it flipped a pivot irrigation system. It destroyed a small outbuilding and damaged other smaller buildings nearby. Several power poles were snapped along highway 79 and the intersection of 79 and route 848.

Shortly after 9pm on November 20, 2025, an EF-1 tornado touched down just east of State Highway 135, approximately 2 miles northeast of downtown Jacksonville, TX and 2 miles southwest of Tecula, TX near the intersection of County Road 4212. Here, the tornado was at its strongest, producing winds around 100 mph and destroying a large barn next to a residential home. Metal roofing was thrown several hundred yards to the northeast while also puncturing a large tree trunk, and nearby trees were snapped and powerlines brought down. Then, along County Road 4212, a carport was thrown on top of a garage and a
neighboring manufactured home had its back porch blown off and thrown into the yard. Continuing east down County Road 4212 there were numerous trees uprooted and large branches snapped. As County Road 4212 then merges into County Road
4213, another barn was destroyed, along with the roof of a carport blown onto the driveway of a residence. Further north along County Road 4213, the were multiple large uprooted and large branches snapped. A nearby manufactured home also displayed significant roof damage. The tornado then lifted within a field nearby the railroad tracks that run north back to State Highway 135.

A tornado touched down overnight in western Hinds County, in the vicinity of Betigheimer and Canada Cross Roads. NWS field survey teams found damage supportive of EF-0 rating in an area concurrent with radar-derived tornado debris signatures (TDS). The tornado moved generally just south of due east along Canada Cross Road which becomes Bill Strong Road east of Middle Road. Several trees were downed along the path with some of the trees having snapped trunks. Inspection of the trees and consultation with local officials confirmed that the snapped trees were dead or otherwise weak. For this reason, the tornado was rated at EF-0 for peak intensity despite the snapped trunks. Otherwise, damage was confined to vegetation and mostly smaller limbs. The tornado lifted along Bill Strong Road after travelling nearly two miles along the road way. The tornado was estimated to have maximum winds of 75 mph, was on the ground for approximately 1.75 miles, and had a maximum width estimated at 100 yards.

The tornado began in a wooded area just north of the intersection of Highway 269 and Flat Top Road in far west Jefferson County. It continued eastward crossing Flat Top Road, Alexander Road, and County Road 45 near the Miller Steam Plant. It continued eastward across Interstate 22, with the most concentrated tree damage along this portion of the path occurring as it crossed Highway 5 near Graysville. Damage primarily consisted of a narrow path of downed trees. A couple outbuildings were also damaged. The tornado crossed Lynns Crossing Road, with sporadic damage continuing to Swann Rd in Mt. Olive. The most notable and concentrated damage occurred in the vicinity of Posey Circle and McCravy Lane in Mt. Olive, where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. Some of these trees fell on homes, causing major damage. Some outbuildings were damaged or destroyed at various points along the path. The tornado then moved northeast, ending at Interstate 65 on the north side of Mt. Olive. Surrounding the tornado path, many trees were damaged or knocked down due to straight-line winds along the bowing complex of thunderstorms. Special thanks to Jefferson County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

A swath of damaging wind occurred across portions of Warren County on the evening of December 18th. Damage was sporadic across the region, consisting of trees and tree branches down, some broken power powers, several sheds blown over at a local business, and several other farm outbuildings with metal roofing peeled off by the wind. There were also a few trees that fell on either houses, farm outbuildings, or sheds.
