Here, as many as 30-40 large trees were uprooted, with several hardwood trees also snapped in the midst of these uprooted trees. As the tornado continued eastward, it snapped a couple more pine trees on the north side of Prospect Church Rd. The last damage observed was to the west of Tommie Thompson, with the tornado appearing to have lifted by 7:29 AM.

EF-0 tornado with peak winds around 85 mph began just west of the intersection of P Drive South and 18 1/2 Mile Road. The damage path ended near N Drive South between 20 Mile Road and 21 1/2 Mile Road. Several trees were uprooted along the path, and some unhealthy trunk snaps. There was minor damage to some structures, including a roof off a chicken coop, and an exposed farm outbuilding with some walls collapsed and metal roof material scattered downfield. The end point had an uprooted tree or two, but also numerous trees that had limbs recently torn off presumably not associated with the tornado, as the only torn limbs were those hanging over the road right-of-way.

Two separate storm chaser videos showed a brief tornado occurring in a field near Kensington Avenue and S 1000W Road in Kankakee Township. Swirl patterns identified in a field from Gray Sky satellite imagery were used to identify the start and end locations of the tornado. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

Per high resolution satellite imagery of damage in a heavily forested area, a new tornado track began just near the intersection of Hardinsburg Rd and Fields Rd. This track briefly crossed Saint John Rd, but missed any structures there before entering another forested area. The first structural damage along this path was along Tyson Ln near Brizendine Ln where a barn hit the threshold of visible damage. Another open air barn along Brizendine Ln had its roof thrown into a wooded area west of the barn. A little farther downstream towards New Salem Church Rd there was additional structural damage. 

This tornado crossed into Meade County near Rineyville Rd. A bigger tree fell onto a house in the Country Ct area. The tornado took a leftward turn, heading north mimicking a turn in the tight mesovortex seen on radar imagery. It caused damage at the Meade County Bank near the intersection of Flaherty Rd and Joe Prather Hwy.  Damage was observed to trees and some houses along Camelot Drive and Rabbit Run  Road.  The tornado continued across fields and did extensive damage to a farm beside Fort Avenue.  Multiple farm buildings were significantly damaged with roofs lofted across Rabbit Run Rd east of Fort Avenue, where the damage appeared to end.

It should be noted that an advanced spotter on base at Fort Knox reported seeing broad rotation as the storm passed his location, but with no contact with the ground. He sheltered in his basement as the storm passed and heard debris hitting his house.  After heading out he saw large limbs in his yard from a tree across the street. Then he observed with a handheld anemometer a 76 mph wind gust behind the first wave, likely with a rear flank downdraft surge.  As of this writing, no damage has been noted connecting this third tornado or the downdraft surge in the narrative below with this damage at Fort Knox. We may yet have further updates here.

Video taken from S 13000E Road south of E 1000S Road looking west showed a brief anticyclonic tornado occurring in a field. Video time stamp and location matches an area of anticyclonic rotation seen on radar imagery. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

The damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified in extreme southwestern East Feliciana Parish, near Lindsay, LA. This tornado caused predominantly minor tree damage including evident displacement and damage of trees consistent with maximum estimated winds near 80 mph. The tornado tracked from King's View Circle through Highway 964 and Thompson Rd before evidently dissipating over open rural fields near the parish line. This damage path was closely located with a strong area of rotation on KHDC radar imagery.

Survey Summary:

A line embedded supercell developed and tracked over north-central
Maryland during the late morning into early afternoon hours on
Monday, March 16, 2026. This storm was part of a much larger system
that brought multiple rounds of severe weather to much of the
eastern United States.

Rotation was evident within the storm around 2000 to 3000 feet above
ground on the KLWX WSR-88D radar, prompting a Tornado Warning as the
storm moved from Frederick into Carroll County. The FAA TDWR TBWI
showed this rotation quickly strengthen and lower to below 2000 feet
just to the southeast of the mid-level mesocyclone being sampled by
the KLWX WSR-88D. The tightened lower-level rotation persisted on
TBWI for 1 to 2 minutes after the mid-level rotation on KLWX had
notably weakened.

It was beneath the tightening low-level rotation at around 12:02 PM
EDT that the first evidence of tornadic damage was found. Several
trees in a weakened state just southeast of the intersection of
Hawks Hill Road and Beth Way snapped near the trunk, and fell toward
the east, west, and north. The parent storm motion was northeast.
The trees that fell were only around 100 feet apart at most, with an
undisturbed landscape around it indicating an initially very narrow
vortex perhaps no larger than about 25 to 50 yards in width.

The tornado then crossed through open fields, lifting the south end
of a long irrigation system and rolling it about 100 feet toward the
north just east of Winters Church Road.

After this, the circulation continued northeastward crossing several
more fields and groves of trees, as well as Little Pipe Creek. The
next visible and accessible damage was noted as the tornado
approached and crossed MD-75 Green Valley Road near the intersection
with MD-84 Union Bridge Road. Here, a couple dozen trees fell in
opposing directions (southeast, northeast, east, northwest, and
north). One large tree toppled onto power lines taking down a power
pole and briefly trapping a motorist between the downed wires, pole,
and downed trees. Several large pine trees at the intersection had
their tops sheared off, falling toward the north, northeast, and
east. Two trees on a hill just east of Mill Dale Lane fell toward
the north-northwest, likely just outside the circulation but in its
inflow as it passed across MD-84 Union Bridge Road. Meanwhile, an
outbuilding just to the southwest of MD-75 Green Valley Road
suffered a near total roof collapse, with the west-northwest facing
walls partially collapsed inward. Similar to the trees off Mill Dale
Lane, this outbuilding may have been just outside the tornadic
circulation, with the damage a result of inflow winds into the
vortex as it passed. It is at this point where the tornado reached
its largest and strongest, with an estimated path width of 150 yards
and peak winds of 80 mph. Despite the extent of the damage, only
about one-third of the trees in its path at this point sustained
visible damage, with no other visible damage to other outbuildings
or the farmhouse at the nearby farm.

A video taken from the Carroll County Emergency Operations Center
showed a swiftly rotating lowering, likely the tornado in progress
as it approached and crossed the intersection of MD-75 Green Valley
Road and MD-84 Union Bridge Road, just northwest of their facility.
Although trees in the foreground obstructed the view and could not
confirm ground contact, the video was directly coincident with radar
and the observed (convergent) damage.

A few trees had their tops snapped off just northeast of MD-84 Union
Bridge Road, but no visible damage was noted beyond this point. It
is possible, based on the rotation signature on TBWI, that the
tornado could have persisted for up to another mile over open
fields, but the path length in this survey can only confidently
conclude a path up to this point, approximately 1.68 miles in length.

The National Weather Service Baltimore/Washington Weather Forecast
Office thanks Carroll County Office of Emergency Management for
their assistance. Additionally, thanks to the trained spotters,
media, and public that sent in reports of damage.

Survey Summary:

A supercell thunderstorm moved through northern Montgomery,
northwestern Howard, and southeast Carroll Counties in Maryland
during the evening hours of Wednesday March 11, 2026. The bow echo
and associated downbursts/thunderstorm wind gusts caused sporadic
tree damage from 60 to 80 mph gusts, and created both a brief EF1
tornado near Cooksville in northwestern Howard County for which
there is a previous report, and this EF0 tornado in Prospect Hills
MD, in southeastern Carroll County in the Patapsco Valley State
Park.

As the storm crossed into southeastern Carroll County, it
produced a brief tornado in Patapsco Valley State Park, with an
EF0 touching down at 7:14 pm. In the park, just east of
Marriottsville Rd, there were numerous trees uprooted and snapped.
The most intense area of tree damage was right along the entrance
drive in the McKeldin Area. Peak winds in this area were
estimated to be 80 mph. Several trees were snapped down in
multiple directions in a path up to 75 yards wide. Shortly after,
the tornado lifted at 7:15 pm and no further tornadic damage was
noted. However, sporadic wind damage in the direction of storm
motion continued to occur with the winds from the severe
thunderstorm.

Special thanks to Montgomery and Carroll County Offices of
Emergency Management for their assistance and damage assessments.

A survey of damage indicated a brief tornado was confirmed within a swath of wind damage south of Banquo. The circulation touched down just east of S 100 W35 and N of E 700 N in far southwestern Huntington county. It moved quickly southeast, causing extensive damage to a converted animal barn as well as a grain elevator on the property. Some tree damage was noted and a few projectiles were observed in 2 different roofs. The tornado cause tree damage to a residence as it crossed into Grant county. Additional tree damage was located on E 650 N, east of Indiana 9.  Debris from the pole barn was found all the way through the track.

A brief tornado began just west of Granny Creek road southwest of Fredricktown. The tornado ripped off part of a metal roof of a barn and carried it southeast, with debris scattered across a field on the east side of the road.

The National Weather Service has confirmed a tornado near the city of Kenton in Hardin County, Ohio. The peak wind estimates were near 90 mph, resulting in a lower end EF1 classification. Some damage points were caused by winds estimated to be closer to 80 mph or higher end EF0. This tornado occurred during the evening hours on Thursday, Mar 26, 2026. 

There was a cluster of storms approaching northern and western Hardin County, in which an outflow boundary began causing power line damage near 8pm. As the cluster of storms continued moving east southeast through the county, wind damage occurred near Alger which was more conducive to straight line winds. 

When the final storm of the larger complex of storms pushed toward Kenton, it produced a brief tornado at the Hardin County Fairgrounds just south of County Road 140, with minor roof damage first observed. Several wooden power poles were damaged and even snapped completely in half. One hardwood tree was also completely snapped on the northern side of the fairgrounds. One building experienced a major loss of metal roofing panels and another building had its concrete block siding blown out, causing a partial collapse of the roof. There was also uplift of an open-ended barn structure, in which large support poles were lifted and shifted slightly from the ground. The final damage occurred on the eastern side of the fairgrounds with additional power poles snapped and minor roof damage to additional buildings. 

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Hardin County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this damage survey.

The tornado began northeast of Mount Gilead along US 42 near Home Road, causing extensive tree damage including multiple snapped and uprooted trees. The tornado continued southeast crossing Township Road 103, causing sporadic tree damage. The tornado then crossed OH 95 near Township Road 110, destroying a 60ft by 100ft outbuilding. Debris from this outbuilding was thrown 100-200 yards to the south southeast by the tornado before the tornado ended.

Scattered tree and some structural damage associated with straight line winds were found both north and south of the tornado track, consisted with straight line winds up to 75 mph.

A weak, very narrow circulation developed along E 1100 S, east of S 600 E and moved quickly towards a home where the southwest portion of the roof was removed and thrown to the northeast. A small building was tipped and rolled towards the north and extensive leftover corn stubble and corn combs were noted in the yard and also carried to the north, landing on the east facing side of the home.

A swath of straight-line winds was evident via high resolution Planet satellite imagery that occurred with a line of severe thunderstorms east of Pleasant Grove and north of Highway 84 near Van Hoover West Road. An approximately 670-yard-wide swath of tree damage was evident west of Van Hoover West Road generally in the 60 to 70mph range. The swath of winds narrowed but became more intense east of the road with peak wind estimates around 80 to 90mph.

High resolution satellite imagery revealed an EF1 tornado began along Waynesboro Shubuta Road tracking east-southeast for roughly 2 miles. The tornado primarily damaged forest reaching a peak width of 200 yards just east of Waynesboro Shubuta Road. A couple older outbuildings appeared to have been damaged to destroyed via high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado lifted shortly after crossing Yellow Creek Church Drive.
This tornado began near the intersection of Charlie Green Rd and Blackledge Rd, producing tree damage along its path. It continued eastward into Wayne County.

Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a brief EF0 tornado occurred west of Lucedale just off of Country Hill Road. This tornado likely began further west with the start point being approximated based on radar data showing a tornado debris signature beginning in the vicinity of the ponds west of Country Hill Road. The tornado remained solely within forest causing minor tree damage.

Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a brief EF0 tornado occurred solely within forest just east of FS Road 342 near Janice. The tornado caused minor tree damage to the forest for roughly a third of a mile before lifting.

Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a brief EF0 tornado occurred just southeast of Gatlin Creek Road west of Vernal. This tornado caused just under a quarter mile of minor forest damage, crossing no accessible roads.

This tornado began near Pleasant Hill Dr and Elm Ln in southeastern Lincoln County and tracked eastward crossing MS Hwy 583 in the Ruth community. It then continued along Greenwood Rd and Raiford Trail, crossing Primitive Dr in the Bristerville community, then across Monument Trail and Junction Ln before crossing into southwestern Lawrence County  near the Verna community. It crossed Holmesville Rd and paralleled Verna Rd before lifting near Excell Boyd Rd. Along the path, countless trees were snapped or uprooted, some in large swaths, multiple outbuildings sustained damage, utility poles were damaged, a mobile home sustained roof and skirting damage, and a site built home sustained minor wind damage.

This tornado began near Junction Ln and Ard Trail in far southeastern Lincoln County, crossing Holmesville Rd as it moved into far southwestern Lawrence County. It continued across Woody Rd, WS Cothern Rd, and MS Hwy 44, passing near the center of the Jayess community. It then tracked across Jessie Wallace Rd and Latrell Sanders Rd before lifting just north of the Walthall County line. Along the path, numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, some in large swaths. Utility poles were leaning or broken with several lines downed. Multiple homes and outbuildings sustained roof and siding damage, and a business received roof damage. A poultry farm southeast of Jayess sustained roof damage.

A brief tornado touched down just west of Honeytown Road in Wooster and moved east across three residential properties before lifting east of Honeytown Road. The tornado caused EF0 damage with estimated maximum wind speeds of 85 mph. Damage along the path included several uprooted and snapped trees, with some large branches impaled into the ground, indicating strong localized winds. A car awning was lifted and pushed across a home, knocking down a TV antenna and causing a chimney to collapse onto the roof. Additional impacts included a blown-down fence, as well as roof damage and damage to an external propane tank at another residence.

No injuries or fatalities were reported with this event.

A brief tornado, embedded within a large swath of damaging straight line winds associated with a bookend vortex, touched down southeast of Hicksville, Ohio. The brief tornado caused some minor tree damage in wooded area before destroying a large pole barn on Clemmer Rd. The tornado moved through open fields, before removing much of the roof off a new construction single family home. Surrounding damage throughout southern Defiance County was determined to be from straight line winds of 60-80 mph.

After extensive aerial data sets were captured as well as additional reports of damage given by Hardin, Meade, Breckinridge, and Grayson County Emergency Management, an update is being made to the previous 43.75 mile long track tornado.  This update will break the previously reported track up into 3 separate tornadoes as well as 2 separate areas of straight-lined wind damage. NWS GIS Mutual Aid, using high-resolution satellite imagery, was provided by Tyler Stanfield of the National Weather Service Slidell, LA, forecast office. The U.S. Coast Guard eagerly provided drone imagery over portions of the tracks in Hardin County. Much thanks goes to both Tyler and the USCG for their help finding breaks in the track over some areas that were very hard to get to!

The first report of the tornado came from Caneyville Fire Department of a tornado touchdown observed north of Caneyville.  Damage was observed from high resolution satellite data north of Caneyville with tree damage near Highway 79 to near Choncie Lee Road.  The tornado continued along Hopewell Road in Grayson County near the Caneyville and Millwood areas.  Several farm outbuildings had the roof peeled off, with one farm having wood planks from the barn damage thrusted into the nearby residence.  The residence also had shingle damage.  Max winds of 100 mph were estimated in this location.

The tornado continued to the northeast across Jones Hill and highway 54 to Stones Chapel Road.  Several farm outbuildings and tree damage was observed, including roof material lofted into nearby trees.  The tornado continued across Clifty Church Drive where a farm had damage to several outbuildings where rooftops were destroyed.  At this location, 3 head of cattle were fatally injured resulting in roughly $7K in damages.  Debris from the farm was lofted into the treeline about a tenth of a mile from the property.  

The tornado continued to the northeast toward Lilac where several farm outbuildings on a hill top were completely destroyed.  Wood planks were driven into the ground in several directions and debris was lofted over the nearby hill.  Significant tree damage was observed here as well.  Max estimated wind speeds of 110 mph were observed here.

The tornado continued to the northeast toward Brandenburg road where trees were uprooted.  The tornado crossed Rough River Lake several times, causing some structural and tree damage into Breckinridge County.  It crossed near the triple point of Grayson, Breckinridge, and Hardin counties and into Hardin near Hardin Springs where several trees were uprooted and snapped. Per high resolution satellite imagery the first tornado ended just northeast of Hardin Springs and just east of Mount Olive Rd.

There was a large forested area that was not easily reachable by the ground survey team between the end point of the first tornado and the starting point of this second tornado. A ground distance of 2.4 miles separated these two tracks. Satellite mutual aid helped confirm a clean break in the damage path.

The estimated starting point for the second tornado along this storm's track, per high resolution satellite imagery, was in a wooded area just west of Pierce Mill Rd south of Garfield. Significant damage occurred to a home near Pierce Mill Road, where a portion of the roof was taken from the home above the garage and living space below.  Mud splatter occurred to the front of the home at this location, and a wood plank was thrown backward into the roof above the living room.  Several wood pieces were impaled into the ground at the property. 

The tornado continued north northeast, causing damage in a forested area that opened up into Horn Cemetery.  It then caused structural damage along Constantine Rd. Downstream wooded areas showed evidence that the occluding tornado still caused damage before lifting southwest of Slaughter Rd.  At that point the rear flank downdraft surged ahead and caused damage along a swath just east of this track.

An EF-1 tornado briefly touched down approximately 5 miles southwest of Akers in Shannon County. Strong winds caused the roof of a single wide home to be torn off as well as the windows to be blown in. Other damage included large trees uprooted and healthy trees snapped. A slight westward extension may be needed in the future after review of satellite data.
An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down approximately 4 miles north of Hartshorn in Texas County. Numerous large trees were uprooted, and a few smaller trees were snapped.

Radar data indicated a large area of strong inbound velocity
along a path east of the couplet that caused the third tornado
along that storm's path. Damage first was noted to an open small
barn along Salt River Rd. just south of Four Corners. High
resolution satellite imagery indicated a large incoherent patch
of trees damaged just west of Salt River Rd south of Berrytown
Rd. Additional trees were noted on ground survey damage along
Salt River Rd just south of New Salem Church Rd. Another barn and
silo were damaged near the intersection of Berrytown Rd and
DeWitt Ln.

Damage continued upstream along Rineyville Rd where a larger 
outdoor garage had its roof peeled off. Entering into Meade 
County, EM noted a tree came down across the road, pulling a power
line down with it, along Vowels Pl. Additional tree damage was 
noted along Rolling Hills Road and then further extensive damage 
to a farm along Fort Ave. This is the approximate end point of 
stronger wind damage. KLVX velocity data showed a quick weakening
trend in those stronger velocities even at higher tilts. The winds
likely remained stronger downstream of the damage but did not
cause as widespread of damage.


The National Weather Service again would like to thank Grayson 
County, Hardin, Breckinridge, and Meade County EMA for their 
assistance with the survey, along with the many helpful homeowners
who showed pictures, video, testimony, and access to their 
properties to help with the survey. Again, with the update, we 
appreciate the assistance from the U.S. Coast Guard and NWS 
Slidell!
This tornado lofted a corn crib, snapped trees, bent an auger, and partially destroyed a roof on a farm outbuilding.

A brief tornado with a path length of less than one mile occurred along Ridge Road between Grand Detour and Oregon in southern Ogle County. The tornado caused damage to a few buildings and trees between Penn Corner Road and Henry Road. One house had approximately two-thirds of its roof removed by the tornado. This was the most significant damage that was caused by the tornado, allowing it to be assigned a high-end EF-1 rating.

An EF-0 tornado began one mile west-southwest of the community of Holcomb near Church Road, where it damaged trees and peeled part of a sheet metal roof off of a barn. The tornado tracked east-northeastward across open fields before impacting Holcomb. In Holcomb, numerous trees were uprooted, snapped, or lost branches and limbs; a church had its roof and windows damaged; a few houses suffered minor roofing and fascia damage; and a barn was destroyed. A grain leg also collapsed, blocking the railroad tracks on the east side of the community. The tornado then continued east-northeastward for a little over one mile longer, impacting a property along State Route 251 between Big Mound Road and Holcomb Road before dissipating. Sporadic straight-line wind damage continued for several miles to the northeast of the tornado's end point.

A swath of damage began just as the second tornado along the long-
storm track was occluding.  It ended close to and east of the
area where the third tornado spun up, thus initially appearing
from the ground survey team to be a continuous swath of damage.

The first indication of damage was a tree down near Constantine
Rd east of Horn Cemetery Rd.  The damage path widened near where
Constantine Road intersects with Slaughter Rd, where an open air
canopy was damaged. Several barns were damaged or destroyed just
southwest of Hardinsburg Rd. Additional damage occurred northeast
of that road, along Vertrees Church Ln. No other downstream
damage was noted as the third tornado path appeared to dominate
the damage just north and west of this area.

Radar data from the KLVX 88D as well as the TSDF TDWR indicated 
peak estimated velocities between 80 and 100 kts at around 1000
feet AGL in this region confirming the higher wind gusts that were
able to mix down to the surface here and cause the observed 
damage.

An EF-1 tornado began in far eastern Whiteside County just north of Fulfs Road and just west of the Whiteside-Lee county line, where satellite imagery showed the beginning of a narrow southwest-northeast path of disturbed soil through farm fields. Drone footage taken along Mound Hill Road in Lee County revealed swirl marks in the field to the west that aligned with the path that was evident in the satellite imagery, confirming that the tornado remained on the ground continuously as it tracked into Lee County. The tornado crossed Mound Hill Road, downing a number of power poles and impacting a property on the east side of the road. The tornado reached its peak intensity here, destroying multiple outbuildings and snapping several trees at this property. The tornado left additional swirl marks in a field to the northeast of the property before causing damage to trees, a residence, and a metal outbuilding along and just south of Lenox Road. As the tornado reached Timber Creek Road, it caused damage to a barn, at least one power pole, and several trees. On the north side of the road, the tornado pushed an old barn off of its foundation into a grain leg, causing the grain leg to collapse. A concrete silo was also toppled at the same location. The tornado then continued northeastward, causing tree and roof damage at a property along Peek Home Road, then damaging an outbuilding, a house, and more trees at a property at Penrose Road and Swarts Road. The tornado produced its last instance of damage at the Hey Tree Service facility along U.S. Route 52/State Route 26 southeast of Woosung before dissipating prior to reaching the Ogle County line. Straight-line wind damage was also observed to the south and east of the tornado's track.

An NWS Storm Damage Survey Team confirmed an EF1 tornado with
peak winds of 105 mph and maximum estimated width of 250 yards.
Damage included over ten snapped power poles, over ten
outbuildings and sheds destroyed, numerous homes with shingle
damage, and many trees with large sections snapped.

The tornado developed near Douglas or about 3.5 miles west of Yates City along State Rt 8, where it damaged an outbuilding. It progressed to the northeast causing some damage to an outbuilding and numerous large trees along Knox Hwy 18 just south of 750 N. The tornado also damaged a couple of homes roofing and siding in that area before moving northeast across Knox Rd 2300 E where it did more tree damage before dissipating.

The tornado touched down about 2 miles east of Elba Center where it did some tree damage just south of Knox Road 900 N. It progressed across I-74 near E Knox Rd where it damaged an outbuilding and some trees. It caused additional tree damage along N Elmore Rd and W Swab Run Rd before dissipating near N McClellan Rd. Debris was thrown to the east of there as the tornado dissipated.

The tornado touched down about 2 miles southeast of Williamsfield just west of the Knox County line, where it destroyed an outbuilding. It crossed into Peoria County and strengthened to 110 mph winds as it snapped off 7 large power poles along State Route 78 near the intersection with Hwy 150. The tornado progressed eastward producing tree damage near N Brimfield Rd and N Maher Rd before dissipating.

The tornado touched down about 4 miles southwest of Galesburg where it damaged a few trees before heading northeast toward Galesburg. The tornado did primarily tree damage as it crossed Galesburg and went into East Galesburg. The tornado dissipated just east of East Galesburg.

The first of two tornadoes began west of Dale and north of I-40, near S3340 Road. 
This tornado produced sporadic damage between I-40 and Westech Road, 
just south of Dale. Damage to trees and a few power lines was noted 
as the tornado curved to the northeast. A tree was uprooted just south 
of Garretts Lake Road and US Highway 177 north of Shawnee. The tornado 
dissipated a short time later. The event time is estimated from radar.

A few minutes after the Dale tornado dissipated, a separate circulation was noted on radar, which tightened and moved to the south and southeast. This tornado likely began northwest of the 
Leo Road and Wolverine Road intersection. While moving to the
southeast, sporadic EF0 damage to trees was noted on Leo Avenue,
north of Garretts Lake Road. EF1 damage was assessed to a gas station awning
along Oklahoma State Highway 18 and Westech Road. The event time is
estimated from radar.

This tornado began near the NS 3510 County Road and EW 1140 County Road intersection. The tornado produced tree and power line damage as it moved north and east. EF1 tree damage was noted along EW 1130 Road, just south of Interstate 40, where large tree limbs were broken off. The tornado then crossed Interstate 40 just east of the Seminole Rest Area, before dissipating near E 1120 County Road and S 354 County Road. The event time is estimated from radar.

Multiple reports of a brief tornado in a farm field positioned latitudinally between County Road 500 and State Route 122, and longitudinally between Interstate 155 and Brownwood Rd.  Tornado occurred in southern Tazewell County, approximately 3-4 miles SW of Hopedale.

Open field; no known damage.

Photo credit goes to Andrew Pritchard.

A tornado likely began near Portland Avenue and Interstate 44, on the eastern grounds of Will Rogers International Airport. Moving to the southeast, the tornado damaged an exterior wall and windows of a building on the campus of Oklahoma City Community College. Generally sporadic damage occurred at several residences between May Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue, including damage to roofs, sheds and fences. Several trees and large tree limbs were blown down along the path as well. The tornado likely dissipated just east of Pennsylvania Avenue. The event time is estimated from radar.

A NWS damage assessment determined that an EF-1 rain-wrapped tornado was embedded in a line of severe thunderstorms that went through Defiance during the afternoon of April 4th. Beginning on the southwest side of town, the tornado produced some minor shingle/tree damage. At least one home was likely destroyed due to a fallen tree. Sporadic, significant tree damage was observed through Riverside Cemetery. The tornado then nearly paralleled S Clinton St as it moved from southwest to northeast. The most impressive damage was done near Davidson and S. Clinton St where several trunks were snapped, a branch lodged into a roof, and several wooden transmission lines were snapped. The circulation continued into downtown Defiance, uprooting/snapping trees, and producing minor to moderate roof damage to numerous businesses including a large church, bank, and USPS building, among others. Notable tree damage was done at the Old Fort before the tornado crossed the river confluence. Video footage from residence confirms a circulation made it across the river. Widespread additional tree and roof damage was then noted in the neighborhoods just north of the Maumee River and west of Carpenter Rd. Finally, several trunks were snapped or uprooted in the Eagle Rock Golf Course before the circulation appears to have dissipated.

The tornado started just south of Martz Rd between Rawsonville and Hoeft Rd. It first flipped a hayride trailer and continued northeast toward Hull Rd. EF-1 damage occurred along Hull Rd with the greatest concentration of EF-1 damage along and just south of Hull Rd between Elwell Rd and Bak Rd. This damage included multiple trees uprooted and snapped, telephone poles snapped, and a large barn wall blown out. The tornado continued northeast crossing Sumpter Rd producing EF-0 damage with scattered large tree limbs and power lines downed. The tornado lifted right before reaching Savage Rd.

This tornado snapped/uprooted trees, bent power poles, and damaged several outbuildings along its path. The roofs on 1 machine shed and 3 hog confinement buildings were destroyed as the tornado moved through.

A tornado passed through northern portions of Sterling, with estimated maximum wind speeds around 90 mph. Along the path, damage was done to trees (including snapped) and two garages in the path saw complete loss of their roofs. Minor damage was noted to two church roofs. There was also a 3000 lb rooftop HVAC unit rolled over, consistent with maximum winds of at least 90 mph.

A bookend vortex moving near Cecil Harden produced a brief tornado that crossed East Mallard Drive. Drone imagery showed clear signs of convergence within tree damage in a grove of trees between Meadows Lane and Mallard Drive with 30-40 trees either uprooted or snapped along the short path. Structure damage was limited to minor siding damage outside of damage caused by falling trees. Additional damage was found several miles both upstream and downstream of the tornado but was determined to be just localized areas of enhanced straight-line winds.

Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a brief EF0 tornado occurred in the Turnerville area, tracking across Dixie Road and Salco Road. The tornado caused mainly minor tree damage along its track, reaching a peak width just across Salco Road around 100 yards wide.

Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a weak EF0 tornado tracked from Irvington through the Laurendine area causing sporadic minor tree damage all along its track. The track of the tornado is further supported by the presence of a radar tornado debris signature.

Available high resolution satellite imagery was able to reveal an EF0 tornado tracked north of Interstate 10 near Grand Bay. The tornado began north of Pascagoula Road solely in forest causing minor tree damage. While there is a gap in visible damage on satellite imagery, radar tornado debris signature persists east connecting with another small corridor of tree damage near Ramsey Road and Boe Road. This is where the end point of the tornado is estimated as any visible damage associated with the radar signature disappears after reaching I-10.

Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a brief EF0 tornado tracked along Dawes Road just northeast of Dees. The tornado remained primarily within forest causing minor tree damage along its track. The track of the tornado is also supported by a radar tornado debris signature.

A mini-supercell developed and produced a short-lived, small, but intense EF1 east and northeast of Lindale, TX. The tornado began in a field just south of FM 16 W downing some small tree limbs and snapping the trunk of a pecan tree. At this same location, significant roof damage, consisting of shingle and roof decking loss, occurred to a single-family residence, resulting in a rating of EF1. The tornado downed a few more tree limbs before crossing FM 16 W. A couple of homes in the Woodcrest subdivision sustained minor shingle damage. Home security cameras in this subdivision recorded the tornado's passage.

The tornado continued northeast and crossed Legion Hills Road. In this location, a second single-family home sustained significant roof damage corresponding to a rating of EF1. A large oak tree was also uprooted on this property. The tornado continued northeast sporadically downing large tree limbs. A few more tree limbs were downed before the tornado lifted near the intersection of FM 2710 and County Road 4107.

This tornado was initially confirmed via multiple videos posted to social media by members of the public. Many thanks go to the Texas Department of Emergency Management and the Smith County Office of Emergency Management for their assistance locating damage.
A brief tornado developed northeast of Savanna with maximum winds near 90 mph. The tornado caused tree damage in a convergent path and also tossed and damaged a small shed.

Based on video and radar evidence, a brief, weak tornado occurred in the middle of rural grassland. No survey was needed as there was no damage. Path length 0.1 miles and path width 15 yds. Maximum wind speed unknown.

The track of a short-lived EF-0 tornado was confirmed via a combination of ground survey, aerial imagery, and the existence of a tornado debris signature on KHDC radar data. The tornado is estimated to have touched down between Charlie Lee Rd and Lee Settlement Rd in rural northwest St. Tammany Parish, west of Folsom, LA. Minor damage to tree tops was visible on aerial imagery which was collocated with a tornado debris signature on KHDC. A tree was partially snapped near the base south of Lee Settlement Rd pointed northwest with additional tree debris noted near the road. The tornado debris signature continued to the northeast beyond Lee Settlement Rd, but no additional tree damage was identified. Therefore, this is where the end point of the tornado is estimated to be.
Locations estimated by video and first hand account.

Shortly before 8:20 PM CDT on Monday April 13th, 2026, a supercell thunderstorm, that had previously resulted in an EF-2 tornado in Ottawa, KS, strengthened and developed a second tornado just east of Hillsdale Lake in northern Miami County, Kansas. Initial damage was confined to the campground and park headquarters. The torando strengthend to an EF-1 as it followed W 255th St and crossed Harmony Rd. The Tornado continued east toward the town of Hillsdale, KS. After crossing Hospital Rd, the tornado strengthend to EF-2 with a peak wind estimated to be 115 mph as it impacted a single family home, before doing significant damage to several storage facilities just west of Old KC Rd. The tornado began to weaken as it crossed rural areas, before ending just short of US Hwy 169 north of 255th St.

Path estimated based on first hand account, video, and radar data.  Tornado caused damage to several trees and buildings on one property near the start of the track, but mainly travelled through open fields.
EFU tornado confirmed based on multiple chaser videos and spotter reports. No known damage along its 2.6 mile path. Tornado path determined by radar and video evidence.

Tornado appeared to develop in the Lisbon Oaks subdivision, causing mainly tree damage before intensifying closer to Highway 164.  Tornado was at it's most intense near Indian Grass Lane where it caused damage at multiple businesses.  The strongest damage was to a insurance car shop port that had a well anchored roof that was completely blown off and found approximately 3-4 blocks to the east near Highway 164.  Damage then occurred to a church near Wildwood Way and multiple homes along Conservancy Court.  Tornado appeared to end near Waukesha Ave along Linda Dr.
Based on chaser video. Location approximate.

The tornado begin 2 miles NNE of Hillsboro, continuing northeast for about 7 miles. The worst damage, rated lower EF3 with winds to 140 mph, was to a home on Raese Road NW of Union Center. A large downburst interacted with the tornado downstream of this point as the tornado tracked north and northeast of Union Center with the width of the downburst nearly 1/2 of a mile in spots. After the tornado crossed the Baraboo River, the downburst began undercutting the tornado and eventually caused the circulation to dissipate near Ackerman Road. There was one brief spin-up from the parent mesocyclone about a mile downstream of this point which has been included in the path of the main tornado.

This tornado developed south of W 81st Street S and just west of S 39th West Avenue. The tornado moved east-northeast damaging the roofs of several homes, some severely, destroying outbuildings, snapping or uprooting numerous trees, and snapping power poles before it crossed into Tulsa County near W 81st Street S. In Tulsa County, the tornado damaged several more homes, uprooted numerous trees, snapped the trunks of some trees, and blew down power lines until it dissipated near Highway 75, north of W 78th Street S. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KINX WSR-88D.

Tornado developed NW of Honey Creek Rd and then hit a barn along the road, shifting it off of the foundation.  The tornado then continued southeast toward Waterford, removing sheet metal from a shed along Buena Park Rd.  The tornado then continued through the north side and downtown Waterford where most of the damage was to trees and houses from the trees falling on them.  A few trees were noted to have been lofted and dropped into the Fox River.  The tornado then continued through the east side of Waterford before ending near Highway 36.

Tornado started NW of County Rd ES, west of I-43 south of East Troy where it heavily damaged two barns.  Corn stubble was noted to be deposited from the corn field to the west all along a path through a cemetery up to I-43.  Some tree damage was noted at the Alpine Valley Golf Course.  The tornado then moved along County Road D and caused additional damage to some barns and outbuildings along with trees.  Tornado ended somewhere south of County Rd D and northwest of Valley View Rd.

This tornado developed just east of Highway 69, northeast of Summit, where trees were uprooted, homes were damaged, and power poles were snapped. The tornado moved northeast across Highway 64, damaging numerous homes, snapping and uprooting trees, and snapping power poles. It then crossed Highway 351 and turned easterly along Hancock Street before crossing the Arkansas River and dissipating east of Highway 10. A few trees were uprooted and numerous large tree limbs were snapped in the path east of Highway 351.

Ground contact most of the way, but not always, as there were two or three occasions when ground circulation was not evident for one or two minutes. But video showed it to be entirely from the same parent circulation, hence one tornado.

Tornado started near Grouse Rd east of Briggsville and then tracked to the northeast.  The worst damage was to an onion farm south of County Road O.  The tornado then crossed I-39 and dissipated near County Rd CX. Storm chaser video and photos confirm the tornado.

Brief tornado started south of Beaver Dam and went through a garage near Shaw Hill Rd, west of the Shaw Marsh Wildlife Area.  Other wind damage was noted on the southern side of the tornado path, attributed to straight line winds.

The tornado touched down approximately 3 miles northwest of Gilman Wisconsin and traveled northeast through mainly rural area. Minor damage occurred to outbuildings and trees on the broken 3.5 mile path.
Sporadic damage path along Plank Rd with mainly tree damage.  Some barn/outbuilding damage to roof sheet metal panels in 2 spots.

A supercell thunderstorm developed through 5:30 PM Wednesday evening into southwestern Henry County. At 6:03 PM, this storm resulted in a tornado beginning south of Clinton, MO near the Lake. As it continued northeast into the southeast side of the city. The tornado strengthend to EF-1 with a peak wind speed of 98 MPH as it crossed E. Calvird Rd. The tornado weakend to EF0 before ending near E. Clinton St. and S. 8th St. This was the first of two tornadoes associated with this storm.

EF1 tornado with peak winds of 100-105 mph began east-southeast of Winthrop and tracked into Delaware County to just east-southeast of Masonville. A barn was completely destroyed at the beginning of its 4.3 mile long path. Additional damage to outbuildings and numerous trees was observed. The tornado also crossed U.S. Highway 20 just south of Masonville. The tornado did roll over a semi trailer.

A tornado formed briefly in the occlusion of an RFD northwest of Pearl City. It heavily damaged and destroyed several farm outbuildings, lifted a large farm wagon into an outbuilding, damaging the roof and side. The tornado also snapped several tree trunks and tree damage. Power poles were also snapped as the tornado crossed Illinois Highway 73 before lifting shortly thereafter. The tornado caused EF-1 damage with maximum estimated winds of 105 mph.

This is the second tornado that resulted from  a supercell thunderstorm that developed in Henry county and impacted Clinton, MO. The NWS Survey team found a gap in damage and security video from Henry County Emergency Management confirmed a second tornado developed from the same parent mesocyclone. This second tornado began near E. Lincoln St around 6:09 PM and continued northeast to N. 6th St, following along the Katy Trail and into the northeast side of the city, crossing Hwy 7 just west of the intersection of hwy 52.

An EF1 tornado began just northwest of the Dubuque Regional Airport.  Max winds of 100 to 105 mph was observed.  The tornado caused damage to trees, snapping and uprooting trees along its path.  A newly constructed home had roof damage on three sides of the roof.

The tornado is estimated to have touched down at 2:25PM MT approximately 1 mile south of the Sink Rd./HWY 89 intersection in far northwestern Rich county. The tornado promptly produced EF-1 damage snapping a few softwood trees. The tornado continued tracking north along the terrain into Cache county, increasing in width and producing a notably wider swath of softwood tree damage consistent with an EF-1 rating. The tornado then took a slight turn to the northeast and slightly weakened, producing a few more instances of EF-1 damage to softwood trees before dissipating in far southern Cache county at around 2:27PM. The maximum width of this tornado was 100 yards with a path length of 0.44 miles. Special thanks to the Cache and Rich county emergency managers for the assistance getting to the damage location, and another special thanks to our local spotters for reporting the damage.

A survey of damage south of Coldwater Michigan indicates that a circulation may have attempted to touch down on Sanford Rd, north of Fenn Road where a barn suffered damage with debris thrown to the east, impacting portions of a solar farm with some damage to panels. A few tree tops showed some minor damage from Sanford Rd to near Interstate 69 where it appears the circulation touched down at a business on the southeast side of the Interstate, causing damage to a pole barn on the property. It continued southeast causing tree damage until reaching the area of Dubendorf and Quimby Road where a garage lost its roof, trees were blown down and vinyl fencing around a pool was blown down. The tornado then impacted a pole barn on South Wood Rd, throwing the debris well east into the field before lifting. Maximum wind speeds were estimated in the 85 to 90 mph range.

This tornado developed west of the S 490 Road and south of the W 830 Road. It moved northeast toward Park Hill, crossed Highway 82 and Murrel Road. The tornado uprooted numerous trees, damaged outbuildings, snapped numerous large tree limbs, and blew down power poles. A few trees were uprooted as it moved across Willis Road, then crossed the Illinois River and dissipated after producing more tree damage on the E 785 Road.

A swath of strong straight-line winds affected southeast Trumbull County in Brookfield Township. Damage was observed along Everett East Road from west of County Route 167 to Greensleaves Circle.

Along Everett East Road, winds lifted a trampoline from a backyard, deposited it in a residence's front yard, and blew down a fence. In the Trumbull County Metroparks, on the north side of Everett East Road, approximately 30 to 40 trees were blown down, all oriented toward the southeast. Several healthy trees were snapped at the base of the trunk, supporting higher-end wind estimates.

A large tree was also blown down on the north side of Everett East Road, clipping a home and damaging the roof. Additionally, several large tree limbs fell onto two homes, causing minor structural damage. Other trees were downed on the south side of Everett East Road.

All observed tree damage and debris were consistently oriented toward the southeast, indicating straight-line wind damage. Maximum wind gusts are estimated at about 90 mph.

We appreciate the Brookfield Fire Department's assistance with this survey.

This tornado developed south of Highway 51, southeast of Eldon, where numerous large tree limbs were snapped.  It moved northeast into Adair County and across rugged terrain.  Trees were uprooted as it moved across the 4630 Roads southwest of Christie, and the roof of a manufactured home was damaged.  The tornado uprooted numerous trees and snapped numerous large tree limbs along Highway 62, with more trees uprooted along Cemetery Road and Highway 59, and along the 4750 Road before moving into Washington County, AR.  It moved northeast across Highway 59 near Cincinnati, where numerous large tree limbs were snapped.  Numerous large tree limbs were also snapped as it crossed Rennic Road and Ham Road before dissipating.
Tornado track based mostly on chaser video. It struck one farm, taking tin off a shed and blowing in garage doors. Trees were also broken.

This tornado developed just west of Piney Road, south of the 782 Road, where trees were uprooted. The tornado moved northeast uprooting trees along Piney Road and the 4765 Road, before crossing into Washington County, AR. The tornado crossed the Baron Fork River, and damaged outbuildings, uprooted trees, and snapped numerous large tree limbs along Salem Springs Road. Trees were uprooted or snapped along Highway 59 and Sugar Hill Road, before the tornado dissipated southwest of Lincoln.

This tornado developed southwest of Hatfield along the Black River and churned eastward, causing extensive damage to trees as it roughly paralleled Old Highway 54. Despite the extensive tree damage, damage to buildings along the path was limited. The tornado was embedded within a larger downburst that caused equal, if not greater, damage than the tornado itself. The downburst undercut the tornado after only a few minutes in existence.

This tornado developed northwest of Saratoga and tracked northeast, damaging one outbuilding during its existence. The tornado was witnessed and photographed by multiple individuals. The tornado rolled a truck, with the driver suffering minor injuries.
Tornado began NW of Somers east of the interstate.  It went through the north and east side of the city, through the fire department and near Somers Elementary School.
Tornado began west of Quinney Rd and tracked to the southeast, hitting 4 barns as it tracked across farmland west of Elkhorn.
Estimated start and end points based off radar and end of debris field

The tornado formed on the northeast of Stewartville and traveled about 10 miles north-northeast, damaging numerous homes and farms. Some of the worst damage was seen near Marion Road, just northeast of Highway 52, where multiple homes were severely damaged with roof removal and partially collapsed exterior walls.

Storm chaser observed brief tornado near the intersection of 230th Road and Sheridan Road in Atchison County, KS. Time was approximately 3:08 pm CDT on April 17 as estimated by radar data. Rating as EF-U since no visible damage was observed in this area, according to emergency management.

This tornado developed several miles southwest of Cream and reached its peak intensity quickly as it descended a ridge to the west of State Road 88, where low-end EF3 damage was observed to one house. The tornado tracked onward to the northeast and damaged mostly trees and a few residences along the remainder of its path as a high end EF1.

The tornado touched down about 2.5 miles southeast of Funks Grove where it produced some tree damage along E 400 North Rd. It progressed northeast crossing Hwy 51 just south of Randolph, causing damage to numerous trees along the way. As it headed toward Downs, it caused EF-1 damage to a home several large trees, with estimated wind speeds of 100 mph. As the tornado moved northeast toward Ellsworth, it caused more tree damage and some home damage, with wind speeds up to 100 mph. The remainder of the tornado path were through countryside areas, with tree damage the primary impacts. The tornado dissipated about 1.5 miles from the McLean County line along E 1700 North Rd.

A brief EF0 tornado passed through Viola, IL, with maximum winds around 85 mph. Much of the damage noted along the short path was done to trees, uprooting and snapping some, with tree tops also sheared off others. Some structural damage was noted in town, where half of a house roof was uplifted with insulation scattered along the tornado path. Damage was also done to the north side of a business's brick facade.

A high-end EF-1 tornado began near Stephens Road between Harrison Road and Meridian Road southeast of Harrison, initially causing damage to trees and a few sheds and outbuildings. Video footage from storm chasers documented the tornado becoming fully condensed and growing in size and intensity as it tracked east-northeastward across Favor Road and impacted two farmsteads, causing significant damage to a few outbuildings and snapping and uprooting multiple trees. Additional storm chaser footage showed the tornado intensifying again as it tracked northeastward across Gummow Road and then reaching peak intensity as it impacted a property along Freeport Road. At this property, the majority of an older two-story house's roof was removed, several trees were snapped, and an old barn was destroyed. The footage then captured the tornado making a sharp turn to the southeast and crossing Freeport Road once again before roping out and eventually dissipating in open fields near Owen Center Road.

An EF-1 tornado began near the intersection of Freeport Road and Bates Road southeast of Harrison, initially downing several tree branches at and near a small cemetery. The tornado produced additional tree damage as it tracked eastward along Roscoe Road before entering the west side of Roscoe and reaching its peak intensity as it tracked through the Hawks Point, Crystal Hills, and Oxford Commons subdivisions. There, multiple homes had portions of their roofs torn off or damaged and had sections of siding and fascia peeled off. A few homes also had their garage doors blown in, leading to parts of their garage walls getting blown out. Numerous trees were also uprooted or damaged in these subdivisions. The tornado then continued eastward, knocking down several power poles along Gleasman Road and damaging a nearby farm outbuilding before crossing the Rock River. East of the Rock River, the tornado continued to cause extensive tree damage. Multiple additional houses sustained roof and fascia damage from the tornado as well. The tornado appeared to dissipate just as it reached the Winnebago-Boone county line. Extensive straight-line wind damage was also observed in close proximity to the tornadic circulation, particularly along its southern flank.

The tornado appeared to start north of School Section Rd and west of Old 89 Rd with mainly tree damage going to the east-northeast.  The tornado then tracked along near State Road 11 going east toward Delavan.  About 4 farmsteads had damage to them, including one empty silo that was blown down from about halfway up.  The tornado then continued east-southeast along Hwy 11 and ended near Redwood Ct on the west side of Delavan where it caused some tree damage.

A high-end EF2, possible multi-vortex, tornado with estimated peak winds around 130 mph started along Highway 20, southwest of Lena IL, and tracked through Lena before lifting just southwest of Orangeville. The tornado caused significant damage to trees along its path, including uprooting and snapping trees. When the tornado begun it immediately caused EF1 damage to trees, gaining strength to an EF2 tornado snapping many power poles southwest of Lena.  The tornado turned to the right, into town causing a lot of roof damage and tree damage.  A lot of houses had shingle and siding damage.  The most significant damage occurred on Grove Street, where three houses lost their entire roof structure.  Two of the homes experienced partial exterior wall collapses.  Damage in this area is consistent with 130 MPH winds. In Lena, the damage footprint in Lena is approximately 1250 yards wide. As the tornado moved to the northeast, damage to farm structures was noted.  Even towards the end of the path, the tornado was causing EF1 damage to trees.

The tornado began in a northeast neighborhood of Rochester and traveled northeast into more rural areas. The first portion of the tornado was weak and intermittent with EF0 damage. North of 65th St, the tornado path became more continuous and intensified to produce approximately 100 mph winds with tree and farm outbuilding damage.

This tornado developed near Ranch Road just north of U.S. Highway 60 west of Ponca City. It moved east causing sporadic tree and power pole damage across the south side of Ponca City before crossing the Arkansas River into Osage County. Further information about the damage in Osage County will be available from the NWS Office in Tulsa.

A tornado developed about 3 miles northwest of Glandon, at the end of Pine Haven Road near County Road J, about 4:44 pm in Marathon County.  The tornado produced significant damage to a barn by collapsing the entire top floor of half the barn, pushed a silo off its foundation, and damaged a metal outbuilding by tearing off most of the roof and some exterior walls.  The tornado moved north-northeast, crossing the Lincoln County line around 4:46 pm.  The tornado then crossed County Road X and Highway 64, downing trees and producing significant damage to garages and outbuildings by tearing off most of the roof of a garage. The tornado dissipated 5 miles south of Doering at the end of Elm Ridge Road in Lincoln County around 4:55 pm.

An EF-1 tornado starting in Hancock County tracked east-southeast before turning east through western McDonough County. It tracked just north of Colmar. Along the path was concentrated tree snapping, many at the base, and some uprooted. Structural damage was noted at several outbuildings, including one destroyed. Several power poles were snapped or heavily leaning on the nearby railroad track.

EF1 tornado with max winds speed of 90-95 mph begun just east of the Galena Territories causing damage to the awning of house.  The tornado then caused sporadic tree damage along it's 3.7 mile long path.  Of interesting note, the tornado mainly caused damage in the valley areas where stretching of the vortex likely increased wind speeds.

The tornado began in rural northeast McLean County about 4 miles northwest of Colfax, damaging trees and power poles and power lines. The tornado crossed into rural Livingston County, damaging more trees and a machine shed.

A high-end EF1 tornado developed southwest of Denver IL and tracked through town. Through the path of the tornado, there were dozens of utility poles damaged. When factoring in the rear flank downdraft (RFD), over 50 poles were broken or bent. Many trees were snapped, some in Denver with high concentration. Some structural damage was also seen, largely to facades, windows, and roofs in Denver.

Tornado appeared to begin along Turtle Creek west of Klug Rd and south of County Road M.  The tornado destroyed an open facing barn shed along Klug Rd.  It then tracked to the northeast and caused damage to 3 barns, a garage and a house along County Road P. It then continued to the northeast and crossed Dam Rd before ending near Turtle Creek again.

A tornado developed about 3 miles west-southwest of Ringle, east of Kronenwetter near Martin and Creek Road, at about 4:46 pm. The tornado moved northeast, crossing highway 29 and downing hundreds of trees. It then moved through neighborhoods along and near River Road from Shady Lane to north of Clubhouse Road.  In this area, dozens of homes suffered significant roof damage, with failures of attached garages common. At least three homes 
in this area had complete removal of their roofs with failure of all external walls and several interior walls, consistent with EF-3 damage. Hundreds more trees were downed in this area, with many snapped near the base. Multiple sheds and outbuildings were destroyed. The tornado continued northeast, closely following the Eau Claire River, and dissipated between Gold Dust Road and County Road Z, 5 miles southwest of Hogarty, at about 5:03 pm. There have been no reported injuries or fatalities.
This tornado developed just northwest of Hideaway Marina just west of the Kaw Lake dam. The tornado moved across the marina causing damage to the boat shelters at the marina.

The EF1 tornado formed near Interstate 94 where County Road B nearly intersects about 3 miles southeast of Osseo, WI. The tornado affected rural areas causing tree damage, sometimes extensive acreage, before ending near the intersection of Highway 10 and Moe Rd.

This EF0 tornado affected mainly rural areas southeast of Oslo MN and was on the ground concurrently with another tornado to the west for several minutes. Mainly farm outbuildings and trees sustained light damage along the path of the tornado.

The EF2 tornado affected mainly rural areas northeast of Rochester MN beginning about 5 miles east-northeast of Viola in northeast Olmsted county. The tornado tracked northeast damaging trees and outbuildings. One farm house lost a roof and garage roof portions. The tornado ended in Wabasha county a few miles southeast of Plainview MN.

This tornado developed west-northwest of Blair and tracked east, affecting mainly rural areas.  The track was a few miles north of Blair with mainly tree damage noted. The tornado path became more intermittent at the end and ceased to the west of the Trempealeau/Jackson county line just north of State Road 95.
Storm chaser video shows a brief tornado touching down in an open field 3 miles north of Pecatonica. The tornado was only on the ground for about two minutes and caused no known damage.

This tornado developed just south of Fox Creek Rd. between I-55 and Veterans Parkway, with a few greenhouses damaged along the track. It traveled near Veterans Parkway and into Highland Park Golf Course where it did tree damage. It continued northeast and did extensive tree damage in Evergreen Memorial Cemetery. It continued northeast through the southeast corner of the Bloomington Country Club Golf Course, where it produced more  tree damage. As it moved northeast it broke two power poles on Empire St and then traveled across Veterans Parkway into a housing area. It did significant tree damage as it moved northeast and then broke two more power poles on GE Road. It continued northeast, doing more tree damage as it headed out of Bloomington moving northeast. It snapped off trees about 1.5 miles northeast of Bloomington along E 1750 North Rd, as well as along E 1900 North Rd where it also did significant damage to an outbuilding near the intersection with N 2300 East Rd. As it continued northeast, it did soffit damage to a home, snapped branches, and damaged an outbuilding along E 2100 North Rd. As it passed to the southeast of Pleasant Hill, it damaged the roofs and doors of two outbuildings along E 2250 North Rd then dissipated after it snapped a power pole and a tree about 2 miles northeast of Pleasant Hill along N 2900 East Rd.

This tornado touched down on Old Peoria Rd 1 miles west of Rivian Parkway on the far west side of Bloomington, IL and did just tree damage. It then moved northeast and damaged several metal buildings. As it moved northeast across Normal, IL, it did significant tree damage, especially between Main Street and North Linden Street. It continued to do tree damage as it moved northeast. As it left town, it flipped over a semi on I-55. It then entered Towanda, doing minor damage and ended just northeast of town.

The tornado began along Spring Prairie Road and moved to the southeast. This tornado had an intermittent path with a few trees uprooted, some shingles peeled from the south side of a roof, another roof peeled back on the southeast corner, and siding damage to a garage. The track continued to the southeast with several limbs snapped from the tops of trees, ending near Old County Highway DD north of Highway 11.

An NWS survey concluded an EF0 tornado caused damage to a building on 83 and Highway MM southeast of Warsaw. This tornado is also reported to have damaged trees in the area which was confirmed via Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis.

Tornado started in a mainly open field to west of Highway 83. A few branches were downed. Along the intermittent path, multiple trees were downed in different directions. A port-a-potty was displaced and pushed over. The tornado continued to northeast into in accessible field. No damage noted along Marsh Rd.

This EF0 tornado began near the Dodge and Mower County line before entering rural Dodge County. The tornado caused minor damage to a grain silo and downed several trees. The track continued northeast and weakened/roped out. This tornado was captured in video from MNDOT cameras south of Rochester. Additional adjustments to the track are likely once high resolution satellite imagery is reviewed.

The tornado began over a farm field where a few small limbs were downed. The tornado continued to the northeast, snapping a few trees and downing several large limbs. Further to the northeast, the view was not accessible with the tornado ending southwest of Big Muskego Lake, south of the Big Muskego Lake Wildlife area.
Tornado started near 6 Mile Rd west of Raynor Ave and tracked to the northeast, ending in southern Milwaukee county.  Possible that this tornado merged with the other one directly to the south.

Tornado started near Raynor Ave and tracked to the northeast while crossing 5 Mile and 6 Mile Rd before ending near 7 Mile Rd.  Most damage was minor but some sheet metal was lofted from a barn. Tornado tracked just to the east of the Milwaukee Airport Terminal Doppler radar.

A tornado tracked ENE across western and northern portions of Saybrook. A narrow, one block damage path consisted of several downed trees and multiple broken large tree limbs. The narrow path and few available damage indicators resulted in inconclusive evidence of a track extending farther to the WSW or ENE into Gibson City.

The tornado set down west of the farmstead and collapsed an empty, 90 ft concrete grain silo. It also blow out the east side doors of a machine building and two north wall panels. The tornado likely continued to the east northeast, ending 2 miles away.

A survey of damage near the Indiana/Michigan state line confirmed as disorganized tornado touched down on Adams Rd, between Mayflower and Portage Rd then quickly tracked across Portage Rd into 2 subdivisions on the east side of Portage Rd. Pockets of tree damage occurred with the majority of any structure damage caused by falling trees. The tornado lifted east of Alpine Ridge Ct. Maximum winds were estimated at 80 mph.

This long track tornado spanned nearly the entire width of Mason County. It touched down in extreme eastern Schuyler County near Bluff City, crossed the Illinois River west of Bath and ended just across the Logan County line in San Jose. Several trees were snapped, and a metal outbuilding blown down, between Bluff City and the Illinois River. In Bath, a few walls collapsed. Along the path, a number of irrigation pivots were overturned, and trees were snapped. Grain bins were destroyed along Peterville Rd east of state highway 97, along with near the intersection of 1300N and 2600E. Some of the greatest damage was in San Jose, where several huge trees were snapped.

The tornado touched down 2 miles east of Table Grove along Rifle Range Rd with a peak intensity of 130 mph when it laid down a swath of tree damage 500 yards wide, snapping off trees up to 2 to 3 feet in diameter just north of Rifle Range Rd. The tornado curved northeast through mostly forested area, where additional tree damage occurred along with some outbuilding damage. The tornado progressed to the east passing north of Bernadotte and Depler Springs before dissipating just north of Bryant. Along its path, the tornado mainly produced tree damage including uprooting and snapping off trunks. A couple of outbuildings lost their roofing material north of Depler Springs.

The tornado began about 3.5 miles northeast of Industry where it did some tree damage followed by snapping of 7 power poles along N 600th Rd. It progressed east between N 600th Rd and N 500th Rd as it produced tree and significant outbuilding damage. The tornado then turned northeast where it did significant tree damage, producing wind speeds around 115 mph. It then crossed into Fulton County along Waters Rd and did roof damage to a home along with more extensive tree damage, snapping off large trees, and destroying a machine shed. It also destroyed a newer grain bin as it moved to the northeast. As it continued to the northeast it likely merged with a newer tornado that came from the south.

A narrow EF-1 tornado touched down near the intersection of W 1700 S and S 350 W roads, where several large tree branches were downed. The tornado then crossed US Highway 41 at peak intensity, downing a billboard, uplifting a large portion of the roof of a restaurant, and pushing over a semi truck. A farm outbuilding was damaged nearby, as well. Debris was thrown nearly 2 miles downstream in an open field just north of US Highway 24. A narrow path evident in satellite imagery in open fields to the northeast of this debris suggested that the tornado likely continued to the northeast for approximately two more miles without impacting any trees or structures before dissipating.

The tornado touched down on the northwest side of Morton just north of the interchange of I-155 and I-74, where it damaged the roofs of a few warehouse buildings. As it reached the intersection of W Jackson St and Detroit Ave it snapped off a power pole and did some damage to business roofs. It progressed east across Morton just south of I-74 producing some minor tree damage along the way before dissipating southeast of Deer Creek. Photo evidence confirmed it was on the ground just southwest of Deer Creek.

The tornado touched down along Runyon Rd about a half mile west of the Tazewell-McLean County line. It cause extensive damage to that area, snapping off 7 large power poles and causing damage to several outbuildings. One large grain bin was tossed several hundred yards to the east. The tornado progressed into McLean County where it caused primarily tree damage before dissipating just north of Woodruff.

The tornado touched down near Lake Windermere where it caused tree damage and some minor siding damage at various locations around the Lake. It progressed to Mackinaw and Heritage Lake where it produced more tree damage. It eventually moved into northwestern McLean County where it snapped of 3 large power poles along N 150 East Road. It dissipated shortly after that.

An NWS survey team found damage associated with a tornado that tracked north of Barnett, MO. Damage included tree debris blown to the east and north, and metal rods sheltering hay bales bent. These results are preliminary, and an additional extension of the path to the northeast and southwest may be warranted with further analysis.

The tornado touched down along Lincoln Blvd on the southwest side of Marquette Heights where it did tree damage and minor home siding damage. It moved east and crossed through McNaughton Park and eventually dissipated along Cole Hollow Rd. While it was on the ground it caused mainly tree damage.

The tornado appeared to start just south of County Road 2200 N in Bureau County, where a barn structure sustained roofing damage. The tornado then moved northeastward into LaSalle County, producing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. Several wooden power poles were damaged just southeast of Mendota before a semi truck was blown over on I-39 as the tornado continued northeastward. The tornado then passed near Meriden, causing additional damage to trees and farm outbuildings before dissipating in an open field northwest of Earlville.

This tornado touched down near the intersection of 1500 North Rd and 550 East Rd, where it damaged two farm out buildings and damaged a tree. As it moved east, it damaged a power pole and snapped the top of a tree off, throwing it 300 yds to the east. The tornado continued to the east, crossing Hwy 51 and then ending on Weldon Springs Rd where it damaged another farm out building and the top of a tree.

The tornado touched down on the west side of Gibson City, producing significant roofing damage to several buildings along 8th Street. The tornado continued ENE for several miles, producing primarily tree damage before lifting approximately 3 miles ENE of Gibson City.

The tornado touched down west of Loda with initial damage consisting of the collapse of two empty grain bins. The tornado continued ENE to just south of Buckley, downing and uprooting trees and blowing over semi-trucks on Interstate 57. Near the end of the damage track, the roof of a large outbuilding was removed, while nearby trees were snapped near the base and deposited in various directions.

The tornado appeared to touch down in an open field southwest of the intersection of E 1200 North Road and N 2450 East Road and impacted a farm, leading to damage to several structures. The tornado then continued northeastward, causing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. The peak intensity of the tornado occurred near the end of the path along the Iroquois and Newton county border, where over a dozen new wooden power poles were snapped at their base. The tornado then appeared to lift just northeast of US-24 in southwestern Newton County.
A tornado moved across the northwest portions of town, mainly snapping tree branches and power poles. One house received some minor roof damage.
The tornado did only tree damage as it quickly moved west to east.

A tornado produced a continuous path of damage from east of Fenwick in Montcalm County to Perrinton in Gratiot County. Trees were snapped and uprooted along the path. Over a dozen barns and outbuildings were heavily damaged or destroyed. About 10 houses had roof damage. Start and end times are based on radar data. The tornado damage was embedded in a larger area of downburst wind damage that was over half a mile wide.

This tornado began near Schermerhorn Lake in Allegan County and was on the ground for around 6.5 miles. The tornado crossed over the intersection of M-40 and 108th avenue before lifting south of 108th Avenue near 24th street. Mostly tree damage occurred along this path. A couple of homes had minor shingle and siding damage and several homes were impacted by falling tree debris. Pockets of thunderstorm wind damage were found south of the tornado path.

The tornado touched down on the north side of the Kalamazoo River along 106th avenue north of Otsego. It crossed into Barry County near Silver Lake and Lake Doster traveling East before lifting near Hickory Corners. Widespread tree damage occurred along the tornado path. Several large barns were heavily damaged and multiple homes and businesses lost roofing material or were damaged by fallen trees. Debris from one business landed on US-131 forcing it to be closed for a period of time following the tornado. Pockets of thunderstorm wind damage occurred just south of the tornado path. Both Otsego and Plainwell had significant tree and property damage as a result of thunderstorm winds south of the tornado path. Thunderstorm damage was also found east of Hickory Corners after the tornado dissipated.

Tornado track and timing based on drone and ground survey and multiple chaser videos. Three outbuildings destroyed. Another shed had much of its roof removed. Several dozen trees were broken or snapped. A house had two portions of the roof damaged, along with some missing shingles.

An EF1 tornado with estimated max winds of 100-105 mph begun roughly 3 miles east-northeast of West Chester, IA. Along its 5.3 mile path, it snapped several power poles and tree trunks, along with ripping sheet metal roofs off of farm outbuildings. A semi truck was also tipped over near the intersection of State Highway 1 and 92, which can be associated with a localized wind surge south of the tornado.

An NWS survey concluded an EF1 tornado touched down southwest of Warsaw, crossing the lake, and tracking just east of Highway 65. The tornado flipped several mobile homes resting on blocks, damaged signs and roofing associated with stores along Highway 65, and created a pattern of tree damage including many uprooted or snapped, surveyed through in-person and Sentinel-2 satellite surveys.

Fire department video showed brief tornado southeast of Postville. This tornado is not known to have encountered any damage indicators. Therefore, we are unable to assign the tornado a numerical rating at this time.
Spotters and chasers reported a tornado that lasted for 4 minutes.  With no known damage the rating is an EFU with an estimated path of 1 mile.

The tornado's path began approximately one mile north of Forest City ,along County Road 2800 E, where it first caused substantial tree damage.  It then tracked northeastward through Union, crossing E Manito Rd and damaging a small outbuilding.  Continuing its movement, the tornado entered the south side of Manito, resulting in snapped and uprooted trees and downed power lines.

After crossing north of Hickory Grove road, the storm peeled the roof off a small outbuilding, lofting the debris eastward.  The tornado then crossed into Tazewell County, just southeast of Parkland, where more tree damage and a tipped irrigation system were documented.

The tornado proceeded to cross the Mackinaw River and caused extensive tree damage as it moved toward South Pekin, lifting slightly past the interchange of Townline Road and Towerline Road.
